review_text:
Excellent build quality. As the selling point of these suggest, these are in fact great when it comes to bass, they're not lying. However, the real selling point of these should be how well they're built. These headphones are the longest I've ever had a pair without them breaking. The only con in terms of build quality is the adhesive on the ear cushions started to decay, but some glue fixed that no problem. The big con, which isn't a con of the headphones themselves really, but because all these aux wires are made in China, they all fall apart absurdly fast. I go through 1 aux wire about every month or two, unless I get really lucky and get a decently made one (by China standards) that'll last a few months. I'm not being overly rough with them, I just use the headphones A LOT and the quality of the cables suck so, very easy to destroy them.

Now, over all audio quality. I'm picky about my audio quality. Picky enough where I can't stand not having an equalizer I can tweak to my liking, but I don't think it's quite fair to call myself an audiophile. That said, the over all audio quality seems fine to me. I did have a headset that was cheap, but supposed professionals were claiming they had really good audio quality despite the price. Comparing the two, I can tell a difference in audio, but not so much in quality. I couldn't tell you which ones sound better over all, I think it comes down more to preference unless you're doing super high end professional work where it's an absolute must to have sensitive headphones to pick apart audio at the seems. The main thing I seek in audio is heavy bass and these deliver, the non-bass audio sounds perfectly good too so over all I'm very happy.

I like these headphones enough that I ponied up for one of the expensive wireless upgraded versions of them, but if you're on somewhat of a low budget and these are available, I'd recommend them. Maybe I'm just lucky, but they should last a good while.

review_text: VERY good sound for reasonable money!. These earbuds have great sound quality, if worn properly. Pay no attention to those who say that they have no bass or that they sound tinny or have too much treble. They, most likely, are having trouble getting a good seal in their ears with the medium sized gel tips that came on the earbuds. They may have missed the little package that has the larger or smaller gels in it. If you don't hear good bass, try the larger gels, if they hurt, try a smaller gel. These earbuds have great sound with punchy bass and balanced mids and high tones. If you like more bass than you get with a correct fitting to your ears, try playing with your phone's music player equalizer settings. I haven't had a problem with them falling out of my ears (possibly another fitment issue for some) but I don't do a lot of bouncing around, either. Any trouble keeping them in the ear could be cured with a set of Comply Sport T200 foam tips if you know the correct size of tip you need (find the correct size gel and you have the right size foam tip.) These earbuds don't have complete sound isolation, meaning that depending on your music volume, you can still hear most things that go on around you, which can be good or bad depending on your particular situation. The isolation foam tips by Comply can fix this, also. The button will pause/play your music, answer/hang up a call, and can select the previous or next track when using the Smart Key app available in your app store for Iphone or Android phones. There is no volume control on the earbuds, but there IS one on your phone or music player, so what's the big deal? These are great earbuds for the price. I am a musician and audiophile. You can pay a LOT more and not get better sound than with these Sony MDREX 110AP earbuds. Better sound CAN be had, but I don't have that kind of money! Believe me when I say that these will do the trick!

Best headphones I've ever used.. again!!!. I owned the original M50s already. Gave them to my brother after he had a fire in his bedroom. The ear cups may be getting a little worn/cracked but they still sound as amazing as the day I got them, and that's how good the M50xs sound too. Comparing the two, I certainly like the multiple removable cords, and the ear cups feel even softer and more comfortable than before. Very high quality! The dark green color is also gorgeous!

The sound.. really just can't be beat for the money (or by most pairs 2x more expensive). If all you care about is bass, then you may disagree, but the M50xs still have plenty of bass. Want more? Best Headphones. Best Company. -Customer for Life After Getting These-. I previously owned a pair of excellent $350 Monitor Headphones from a German company. I wanted something from a company that had great expertise in headphones and payed attention to ALL of the details to make their product and headphones the best in all aspects. Hence, I checked out Audio-Technica and I got what I was missing out on:

1) These headphones are much more comfortable for LONG USE, which is a must in a solid pair of headphones.
2) ELEGANT DESIGN (I got the DG Limited Edition). Absolutely fantastic look for PROFESSIONAL headphones that offer Amazing sound.

3) The reason that I want to mention that the noise cancelling is great, just as you would expect, is because at the same time they are VERY comfortable - especially the ear pads.

4) The Sound Quality is absolutely PHENOMENAL, I mean I can't tell the difference between my old $350 pair. I got MORE than what I payed for with these Mx50's. Love it.

5) Finally I love the fact that they have included the option to attach different chords. The thing is they are VERY smart for doing this because over time(years) the chord may break while the headphones will still be at 100% - we especially know this to be true with other cheap branded headphones, where the chords break all the time and much much sooner than many years. This way you will have these headphones working forever, so you might as well merry them now.
-Also, the attention to detail is exhibited again when you notice that you get 3 chords that are all useful: For example, they offer a short cord that is perfect for use anywhere for casual listeners and great for travelers. The other 2 are also specific to professional studio listeners but can be used by anybody (you can take advantage of the long cord and screw on adapter).

6) Well one last and Most Important thing is the EXTRAORDINARY BUILD QUALITY! I love this, as for me this is most important in any product that you use and are rough with everyday.

.

review_text:
No Artificial Colors or Flavors. What do I mean by the title? Unlike some other high profile and popular headphones, one with a big B (Bose) and the other with a little b (beats), the M50x's are natural. No modifications for extra bass or treble. That only robs you of hearing things you should be by drowning them out from boosting other things. These give you the pure, unaltered sound as the artist intended. That means a lot to me because as a home theater enthusiast, I want to see and hear things as they were meant to be. I want accuracy in my audio and video devices and these deliver the audio in spades. It reminds me of TV displays in stores. The brightness and contrast are cranked up to get your attention but upon closer inspection, it's not at all realistic. Details are lost, people look sunburned, blacks look grey and it doesn't reflect real life. That's what Bose and Beats are to me. Dial back the settings and you get every detail, accurate colors, levels of shadow and an overall realistic picture. That's the AT M50x's.
When searching for my first pair of expensive headphones (I had never spent more than $50) the M50x's consistently came up as the best or one of the best in the under $200 category. $200 was all I was willing to spend. What always caught my attention was the unaltered clarity these provide and so far, I have been very pleased by how well they deliver on that promise. When listening to music, I can clearly focus in on every instrument, every cymbal, every word, chorus and solo. It's a joy to hear my music so clearly and well defined. If other headphones I've used were good, solid standard definition, these are definitely high definition. If you really listen to your music, these headphones are going to help you do that and will make it a much more enjoyable experience. I've used them for movies as well and they really deliver a convincing movie experience. Dialogue is easy to understand, sound effects pack all the right punches, surrounds come through, putting you in the moment and theres nice thumps and booms substituting for subwoofer action. If there's a need to keep the noise down or your going portable, you can have a great movie watching experience with these.
Speaking of portability, this isn't your practical, walking around town or going to the gym set. They're big but perfect for home, long trips or any other stationary listening. Sure, you could take them out but it's a pretty big set to have on when you're on the move. I'll use my on-ear Noontec Zoro HD's (which I highly recommend) for that.
Build quality is excellent. There's plenty of plastic here but this is a very solid feeling set. The leather on the head band and earpads is soft, comfortable and has an expensive look and feel. The earpads completely cover my ears and form a nice seal, keeping the sound in, preventing excess leaking and keeping outside sounds out. I'm not one of those 8 hour a day wearers but for the duration of a movie, I didn't notice any discomfort. Felt or suede earpads can always be purchased and swapped out if need be. They're also very versatile by how many ways they can contort and collapse for storage. I also like the matching and locking removable cord and spare cords packed in the box. Also packed in was a soft leather pouch in a matching chocolate brown to my set. I bought a hard case to use instead but I could see using it for a short trip or days use elsewhere. I went with the limited edition dark green and brown and they really look nice. The green is a dark forest green, almost black in low light and the brown is a darker chocolate brown, with champagne gold accents on the ear cups and hinges. Aesthetically, this is a very good looking and feeling combination. Like they're more expensive than their price point.
I chose the combo from Beach Camera as you get the free case and mini amp for the same price. Shipping was next day and reasonable and packaged well.
Overall, I'm very satisfied with this purchase. I read a lot and watched a lot of videos before making the decision to buy these. It only took a few listens to know that I made the right choice. I know there are other brands of good sounding and well built headphones in the same price range but this combination of high marks by professional and casual reviewers, numerous appearances on top 5 lists, good brand reputation, warranty, build quality, and physical attractiveness made these the set for me. When I give a 5/5 review, it's not for perfection or best available product, it's for a performance and value combination. These meet that combination easily. Highly recommended for music listeners.
Note: I've since added dbrand skins and Brainwavz earpads to mine for that custom look and feel. Definitely recommended for M50x owners.

review_text:
Beats Wish They Sounded This Good. I came to this headphone after having used and loved a pair of Shure SRH-440 for the last few years. Those headphones impressed me with their flat-tuned response, nice sound stage, comfort and durability. After my 440s were stolen from my desk where I work (word of advice: don't leave your headphones out over a weekend for the cleaning crew to steal), I decided to step up and go with the ATH-M50x. I've only had them for 1 day, but they are outstanding right out of the box. They have a more curved eq response overall than the SRH-440s with more defined bass, but certainly not to an obscene degree and not at the expense of any higher frequencies. The sound stage is rich and wide - much moreso than the SRH-440. They are reasonably light and fit comfortably over the ears with very good outside ambient noise isolation. They are a little tight at first, but I know from prior experience that they will loosen up over time a little.

Having previously spent over 10 years working in the consumer electronics industry, I can confirm that these are among the best and definitely a nicer-sounding set of over-the-ears than Beats. These outperform Beats and most other headphones in a similar price range on pretty much every level and, at least to my adult eyes, look classier too. Easily the best pair of over-the-ear headphones I have ever owned!

review_text:
Superb. Headphone sound is a very personal thing. How do you tell whether the AT's are the best for the price? Youtube! Lots of videos on independent tests and a user blind test. Electronics articles. AT's are rated among the top choices by almost all audio writers and professionals. So, I took the plunge, looking to upgrade from MMElectronics open headphones to a closed system to block out extraneous noise. Frankly, the MME's have very good sound for a reasonable price ($40) and I will continue to use them when outdoors or using an iPhone. But the AT's are an order of magnitude above these entry level phones.

The M50x sound quality is superb. Clear sound over all frequencies. Perhaps a bit bright in the HF's, but most of us like brightness. The bass is full but not booming. These aren't Beat Studios with their bass attenuation.

Overall, I don't think you could ask for a set of headphones in this range that will do any better. They reproduce what is recorded very accurately.

My favorite test is Faltemeyer's "Axel F". About 50 seconds in, there are small clicks that have a tendency to get lost with less responsive headphones. The AT's provided clear definition.

review_text:
Excellent for the money, but over-hyped and need a 3rd-party cable. I bought these as an inexpensive alternative to the ATH-MR7 headphones, which I bought a few months ago. As much as I love the MR7s, I'm not sure I'd want to ride the New York subway with them on. In addition to being much less expensive, the ATH-M50x has a much more flexible design that allows them to be folded into a more compact form for travel. That said, they use a non-standard locking 2.5mm headphone jack that requires use of the proprietary cords that come with the headphones. Designed as a studio monitor, these phones were not intended for use with a smart phone and the supplied cords lack even a microphone, let alone controls. Suitable replacement cords are available from third parties, however, so that is not a significant issue.

My quibble with these cans, however, is in sound quality. Although I would agree that the sound is exceptional for the price, There are other headphones in the price range that are nearly as good, and with a frequency response that is more to my taste. The high end of these is much better than most of the competition, but it's not in the same league as the ATH-MR7s. I find the bass response of the ATH-M50x, however, to be excessive and boomy - not something I was expecting from a studio monitor. Don't get me wrong - these are excellent headphones, but not nearly as exceptional as all the reviews would lead you to believe.

review_text:
Love bass heavy headphones? Get these!. If you are looking for BASS HEAVY headphones on the cheap (let's say, for the gym, running, school), get these!

I was looking for a replacement for my bass-heavy Sony MDR-W014 for a very long time. I run every day to HOUSE music (shout-out to Miss Monique for knowing how to DJ like a bawse) . I noticed that when I fire my EQ on my Android devices (OPO, Pixel XL) the ability of many headphones to shoot out bass is weak. Some can't even handle any EQ other than flat. Shame.

Decided to give these a try and I am super happy. I don't understand how they managed to kick so much bass out of these. My EQ is back to where I like it: bass is all the way up.

One caveat though: I noticed that I need to crank the volume all the way up (as opposed to the Sony, which managed about 60% volume). And at about 70% volume, increasing the volume will do nothing. Not sure if this is my phone's dac limitation or the Jib themselves.

My next job: find an even bass-heavier (if that's possible) model from Skullcandy (know any?).

Summery: GET THESE IF YOU LOVE BASS.

review_text:
Always like Gumy's!. Been using Gumy head phones for several years, always like a good pair of Gumys.
Only have a few small complaints.

For the most part Gumys are VERY comfortable, they're light and thin and easy to stick in your pocket, they don't pull on your ears or cause major discomfort like a lot of other small earbuds do.
However, after extended use (over an hour -say a full length movie, or using it for music while working on your next exam) it does seem to cause a bit of discomfort in my ears. BUT!! That may just be the shape of my ear, and it doesn't apply to everyone. ;)

I purchased this specific earbud (coconut white) because I LOVE coconuts and thought a creamy white would be an awesome color to have next! But I was disappointed in the color, it actually looks dirty and cheap, like something my grandma would have picked up at the Dollar Store.

The only other small complaint I would have is that if you use these headphones often (like I do), they slowly start to short out right below one of the earbuds. I generally find that these earbuds last me anywhere from 3-6 months at a time.
Sadly though, it's not just Gumy's, because I have tried different brands, and they all have done the same. (Even Apple's earbuds, though they lasted closer to 9 months, but I still had the same problem with the shortage right below the earbud itself.)

I still choose Gumy though because of the comfort compared to other brands, and the colors. I mean really.. who doesn't love a bright colored pair of headphones? ;)

review_text: Best economical headphone. I picked up a pair of these JVC Gumy Earbuds in Coconut White in a local store for $6.88 on sale. They are about the same size/form-factor as the original Apple earbuds with the exception of they are actually slightly better form fitting to the ear canal. I hardly know they are there. I wear them in the office and they pretty much block out all the distracting ambient noises and conversations, and I can listen at a low volume. The sound is excellent on low volume with plenty of head room to go much louder. They are not "tinny", but rather warm and full sounding and the base response is quite nice. Others have said that the chords transfer noise to the earbuds, but it is only noticeable when the music is turned off. The chord is not as pretty as Apple's single, round chord (it is two affixed side-by-side chords typical of cheaper headphones), but the chord seems tough enough. In fact I forgot them in a shirt pocket and they went through both the washer and dryer, and while the cord was twisted in places, the headphones still work perfectly! For the price I paid I plan on picking up another set as a backup.

review_text: Excellent earbud in the low price category. I purchased all of these and compared them with each other: [[ASIN:B004Y3A3ZQ JVC HA-F150W Gumy Headphones, White]], [[ASIN:B003EM8008 Panasonic RPHJE120K In-Ear Headphone, Black]], [[ASIN:B007FRYDWM JBL Tempo High-Performance Earbud Headphones (Black)]], [[ASIN:B0054L4AD8 AKG K311 In-Ear Headphones (Arctic Blue)]]. All sounded good for inexpensive earbuds, however the JBL and AKG were standouts, with Panasonic next and JVC last. JBL and AKG sounded very realistic with good, crisp treble and audible/realistic but not overpowering bass. JVC treble was harsh. All were comfortable in my medium size ears. AKG and JVC stayed in well while jogging, as did JBL when worn with the removable foam covers. I'd rate the AKG and JBL as tied for best sound. The AKG at about half the JBL price is the winner. I plan to use the AKG, JBL, and Panasonic but will give the JVC's to my daughter! Note that I have heard that these earbuds are often copied by cheap counterfeits from China so buy from a reputable seller like Amazon (some Amazon marketplace or ebay sellers may not be!). Also, individual hearing and sound tastes vary so your review may not be the same as mine. Good luck with your earbud search, hope this review helps!

review_text:
These earbuds survived nearly 5 years of constant torture!. I've been working for nearly ten years at a factory, and have been using an iPod for about 7 of those. My original earbuds wore out within the first two years of use, and I was looking for some cheap replacements that weren't crap. I found a package of these at Wal-Mart or something, and I've used them ever since.

Last night, after five years of nearly daily use, one of the earbuds stopped working due to the cord catching on something and snapping off. A year ago, the left-side earbud was damaged by a piece of work equipment and cracked a bit, but continued working perfectly even with a chunk missing and the gummy bit partially ripped off. With the gummy bit damaged, earwax easily built up over time inside it, and even with my best efforts, still collected in the inner workings of it. The man section of the cord was cut in multiple spots, and part of the rubber rubbed away through constant friction on my clothes/me. It dealt with extremely hot summers and swam in sweat for hours on end, day in day out, sometimes would get caught on things and yanked out, all sorts of damaging instances.

Throughout that whole five years, they never stopped working properly. Not even losing sound for an instant in any of the above cases. It took getting ripped off the cord itself for the earbud to stop working. These are top-quality products. What I'm saying is, there is no better earbud for your money. Thirty dollars for official iPod earbuds when these are what amounts to The Little Earbuds That Could for at most 10 dollars a pair, to pick the former is sheer LUNACY. The Apple ones didn't even last two years.

BUY THESE EARBUDS IF YOU NEED EARBUDS. It's foolish to pay more for crappier ones than these!

review_text:
Always like Gumy's!. Been using Gumy head phones for several years, always like a good pair of Gumys.
Only have a few small complaints.

For the most part Gumys are VERY comfortable, they're light and thin and easy to stick in your pocket, they don't pull on your ears or cause major discomfort like a lot of other small earbuds do.
However, after extended use (over an hour -say a full length movie, or using it for music while working on your next exam) it does seem to cause a bit of discomfort in my ears. BUT!! That may just be the shape of my ear, and it doesn't apply to everyone. ;)

I purchased this specific earbud (coconut white) because I LOVE coconuts and thought a creamy white would be an awesome color to have next! But I was disappointed in the color, it actually looks dirty and cheap, like something my grandma would have picked up at the Dollar Store.

The only other small complaint I would have is that if you use these headphones often (like I do), they slowly start to short out right below one of the earbuds. I generally find that these earbuds last me anywhere from 3-6 months at a time.
Sadly though, it's not just Gumy's, because I have tried different brands, and they all have done the same. (Even Apple's earbuds, though they lasted closer to 9 months, but I still had the same problem with the shortage right below the earbud itself.)

I still choose Gumy though because of the comfort compared to other brands, and the colors. I mean really.. who doesn't love a bright colored pair of headphones? ;)

The buds also have a good, minimalist look to them. They fit comfortably under a beanie too. Very waterproof. Most times I can just blow the sweat out of them and they are ready to go immediately.

review_text:
Very good for the price. I was looking for a replacement for my ipod headphones that had recently died, and I had read mostly good reviews about these earbuds. For under $5 for some headphones, I wasn't expecting much. However, when I got them, they were great!

Of course they're not high quality professional-grade recording headphones by any means, but most if not all of the lows register quite well, and it's a decent balance of lows/mids/highs. Like I said, these are good for watching videos on your computer, or listening to your ipod while working out, etc. I'm sure no audiophiles would get these, but for the price, they are awesome! I might get a second pair just in case.

review_text:
Sound quality is quite bad, especially for listening to podcasts. I'll start with saying that I'm not usually very picky when it comes to audio quality. I always tend to purchase ear buds under the $10 mark as they wear out on me in one way or another in about 6 months to a year because of running with them on. Due to that tendency, I've gotten my fair share of bad sounding ear buds, but these are probably the worst.

I primarily listen to podcasts and these Gumy headphones make it sound like the people were recording from inside a dumpster. Music isn't as noticeably affected, but certainly doesn't sound good. Shopping in the <$10 range for ear buds is really a hit or miss deal, and these are certainly a miss.

review_text:
BETTER THAN APPLE (no, really :-). Yes! They are just like iPhone earbuds--but better!

I hate hate HATE the new earbuds, with the rubber condoms that go in your ear. They never fit and they make me feel violated. I missed these and was debating on buying *yet another* set of iPhone earbuds. I am so glad I found these. They are white (just like Apple) and they look, feel, fit, and sound EXACTLY like Apple. But these have a tiny bit more printing on them. Other than that they are virtually identical. They are a bit gummier (2% gummy, not squishy or gooey). They are not "hard plastic" but more "firm plastic." The sound is incredible, possibly even better than the Apple ones I am always paying too much for.

BY THE WAY: There are no volume controls on the cord. Some earbuds come with those. Just so you know this is not what you are getting. They fit your iPod/iPhone, and even my Samsung Galaxy S3 just fine. There is a term for that kind of jack but I don't know (or care) what it is. All I care about is that they work and they are durable. Given that they are built almost identically to Apple's earbuds I am assuming that they will last as long (which is never long enough). Bottom line: for the price these are a steal.

review_text:
Quality Drop. I've purchased over a dozen of these headphones, and they've always been great.

However, I recently purchased a set of 3 and all were bad (soft washed-out sound with little bass).

Curious as to why the sound quality was so much worse I opened up one of the earbuds and compared it to my aging pair. Sure enough the copper ring around the driver was almost non-existent. It folded in half just picking it up, while the ring from my existing pair was much thicker and took a substantial amount of force to bend. Plus it was much more difficult to open my older pair because it had a much sturdier construction.

It's possible that they've improved and I was sent a set of 3 from a very old batch. Regardless, don't buy them from Online Daily Deals (they apparently have a bad/old batch).

review_text:
Always like Gumy's!. Been using Gumy head phones for several years, always like a good pair of Gumys.
Only have a few small complaints.

For the most part Gumys are VERY comfortable, they're light and thin and easy to stick in your pocket, they don't pull on your ears or cause major discomfort like a lot of other small earbuds do.
However, after extended use (over an hour -say a full length movie, or using it for music while working on your next exam) it does seem to cause a bit of discomfort in my ears. BUT!! That may just be the shape of my ear, and it doesn't apply to everyone. ;)

I purchased this specific earbud (coconut white) because I LOVE coconuts and thought a creamy white would be an awesome color to have next! But I was disappointed in the color, it actually looks dirty and cheap, like something my grandma would have picked up at the Dollar Store.

The only other small complaint I would have is that if you use these headphones often (like I do), they slowly start to short out right below one of the earbuds. I generally find that these earbuds last me anywhere from 3-6 months at a time.
Sadly though, it's not just Gumy's, because I have tried different brands, and they all have done the same. (Even Apple's earbuds, though they lasted closer to 9 months, but I still had the same problem with the shortage right below the earbud itself.)

I still choose Gumy though because of the comfort compared to other brands, and the colors. I mean really.. who doesn't love a bright colored pair of headphones? ;)

review_text:
BETTER THAN APPLE (no, really :-). Yes! They are just like iPhone earbuds--but better!

I hate hate HATE the new earbuds, with the rubber condoms that go in your ear. They never fit and they make me feel violated. I missed these and was debating on buying *yet another* set of iPhone earbuds. I am so glad I found these. They are white (just like Apple) and they look, feel, fit, and sound EXACTLY like Apple. But these have a tiny bit more printing on them. Other than that they are virtually identical. They are a bit gummier (2% gummy, not squishy or gooey). They are not "hard plastic" but more "firm plastic." The sound is incredible, possibly even better than the Apple ones I am always paying too much for.

BY THE WAY: There are no volume controls on the cord. Some earbuds come with those. Just so you know this is not what you are getting. They fit your iPod/iPhone, and even my Samsung Galaxy S3 just fine. There is a term for that kind of jack but I don't know (or care) what it is. All I care about is that they work and they are durable. Given that they are built almost identically to Apple's earbuds I am assuming that they will last as long (which is never long enough). Bottom line: for the price these are a steal.

review_text:
Quality Drop. I've purchased over a dozen of these headphones, and they've always been great.

However, I recently purchased a set of 3 and all were bad (soft washed-out sound with little bass).

Curious as to why the sound quality was so much worse I opened up one of the earbuds and compared it to my aging pair. Sure enough the copper ring around the driver was almost non-existent. It folded in half just picking it up, while the ring from my existing pair was much thicker and took a substantial amount of force to bend. Plus it was much more difficult to open my older pair because it had a much sturdier construction.

It's possible that they've improved and I was sent a set of 3 from a very old batch. Regardless, don't buy them from Online Daily Deals (they apparently have a bad/old batch).

review_text:
So far, SOLID wireless headphones from V-Moda. This won't be a full review yet because I just got my pair a couple of days ago from V-Moda, but so far they are awesome.

Coming from using the M100 religiously, they sound equal to actually significantly better in some areas.

The M100 is great for bass while keeping everything else crystal clear. The Crossfade Wireless seems to improve on the mid clarity while tightening up the bass and keepin it punchy.
This goes for wired and wireless and I honestly can barely tell a difference in sound quality between wired and wireless.

The construction is very much like the M100 and I used my XL ear pads on the wireless. I opted for the gunmetal version and although mines has a blue tint to them I still really like them, they just seem different that I expected.

The pairing was easy enough and I know for my iPhone 6, that the notifications screen shows the battery percentage while the main screen shows a new battery bar by the phones battery bar that shows how much juice the Crossfade Wireless has left in it. I have used them wirelessly for around 5 hours so far and it shows about 60% battery left.

The controls feel good and seem sturdy and reliable. They work a lot like the three button remotes on apple headphones.

I really like that there is a wired mode that immediately shuts down wireless mode as soon as you plug it into a 3.5mm jack. This turns off the battery and allows for unlimited listening in wired mode whereas some wireless headphones always need the battery to be used.

My only issue comes from the M100. Cliqfold and the lack of it. The M100 came with an awesome feature called cliqfold that allowed the headphones to fold up really nice and compact. That feature seems to have been omitted here and I don't see a logical reason why just yet. They are still very portable so I didn't feel it enough to dock a star for.

Overall they are great wireless headphones from a company that initially never seemed like they would make wireless headphones. I feel a lot of time went into tuning and although my experience with wireless Bluetooth headphones is limited, I know these are the best I've heard. These are easy to recommend and I'll keep updating my review as I have more time with them.

UPDATE 1:
Forgot to mention that comfort for the Crossfade Wireless is similar to the M100. With the stock earcups comfort is good but after a few hours it is not great. I recommend the XL Earcups if you experience a good deal of discomfort after long term use. I do have a big head so try out the standard cups first but for me the XL earcups add a lot more comfort.

review_text:
SOLID Wireless Headphone. This won't be a full review yet because I just got my pair a couple of days ago from V-Moda, but so far they are awesome.(edit. week and a half in now and still really liking these.)

Coming from using the M100 religiously, they sound equal to actually significantly better in some areas.

The M100 is great for bass while keeping everything else crystal clear. The Crossfade Wireless seems to improve on the mid clarity while tightening up the bass and keepin it punchy.
This goes for wired and wireless and I honestly can barely tell a difference in sound quality between wired and wireless.

The construction is very much like the M100 and I used my XL ear pads on the wireless. I opted for the gunmetal version and although mines has a blue tint to them I still really like them, they just seem different that I expected.

The pairing was easy enough and I know for my iPhone 6, that the notifications screen shows the battery percentage while the main screen shows a new battery bar by the phones battery bar that shows how much juice the Crossfade Wireless has left in it. I have used them wirelessly for around 5 hours so far and it shows about 60% battery left.

The controls feel good and seem sturdy and reliable. They work a lot like the three button remotes on apple headphones.

I really like that there is a wired mode that immediately shuts down wireless mode as soon as you plug it into a 3.5mm jack. This turns off the battery and allows for unlimited listening in wired mode whereas some wireless headphones always need the battery to be used.

My only issue comes from the M100. Cliqfold and the lack of it. The M100 came with an awesome feature called cliqfold that allowed the headphones to fold up really nice and compact. That feature seems to have been omitted here and I don't see a logical reason why just yet. They are still very portable so I didn't feel it enough to dock a star for.

Overall they are great wireless headphones from a company that initially never seemed like they would make wireless headphones. I feel a lot of time went into tuning and although my experience with wireless Bluetooth headphones is limited, I know these are the best I've heard. These are easy to recommend and I'll keep updating my review as I have more time with them.

Now using these for about a week and a half now, everything has held up. The battery life listening at roughly 50%-75% gets me right around 12 hours. Connectivity is typically fast and responsive and now using it to make calls, microphone clarity is good with moderate background noise and great in quieter settings.

I wanted to point out that for those who are not familiar with the V-Moda headphones, these are not audiophile headphones in the standard sense. These are not neutral headphones. In my opinion they work pretty great for every kind of music you can throw at it but they are tuned for modern music, rock, rap, hip hop, electronic, and so on. The bass is forward and punchy yet clean which takes slightly away from the mid but still sounds fairly clean. The highs are forward but not harsh and overall there is a nice and very fun balance. These are easily the best bass geared headphones I have listened to based on leaving the mids and highs intact. The soundstage is reasonable for closed headphones and while it won't compete with any open air headphones, they aren't meant to. I have listened to rock, classic rock, hip hop, rap, EDM, country, and even classical music without any issues. While they are not my preferred method of listening to classical music, they do a great job considering what these headphones are geared towards.

UPDATE 1:
Forgot to mention that comfort for the Crossfade Wireless is similar to the M100. With the stock earcups comfort is good but after a few hours it is not great. I recommend the XL Earcups if you experience a good deal of discomfort after long term use. I do have a big head so try out the standard cups first but for me the XL earcups add a lot more comfort.

*This review is for the Gunmetal Version

review_text: Incredible sound and comfort. These V-moda headphones are unique in design, comfort and sound. First of all, out of the box, it comes with a case and velcroed into the case is a wire to connect the headphones to the device in case of low power or if you wanted to save battery time. It comes also with a charger cable and, of course the headphones. The packaging is unique with clips and sturdy cardboard. (I am not sure why there has to be such quality with an outer box that will probably be discarded.) There are instruction manuals and warranty guides. The instructions are clear and pairing with your device extremely easy. Once paired, the sound is crisp and clear. The bass is well realized. Clarity is perfect for jazz, classical, or pop. Interestingly, there is no discernible difference between wireless mode and using the wire. I have used the headphones to watch several movies and having them on my ears remained comfortable for several hours. Controls are easy to reach and quite intuitive unlike many headphones. These are the most expensive headphones I own and I can tell by the quality and the sound. I love them.

review_text:
Freedom of cordless beats out the need for EQ. I own a lot of headphones. I am somewhat of a headphone junkie. I own several pairs of V-MODA headphones including the older wired pair of the over the ear Crossfades. They are excellent headphones but they are not my first choice for everyday use. I have been using my Audio technica ATM-M50's as my daily headphones for probably over a year now. Sometimes I switch it up to get a different sound signature but the M50's are just so well balanced that I have a difficult time finding something that can compete in this proce range.

But..enter wireless headphones. I have a few sets including a nice pair of senheiser active noise cancelling ones but I haven't found a great set that was free of soem issue (the Senheisers volume is too low for me). When I was offered as et of these I jumped at the chance because I have had good luck with V-MODA.

Design and comfort - Like the older Crossfades I have, these are some of the most comfortable headphones I own. I can wear these for hours. The design is beautiful and you don;t feel silly wearing them like I do with my M50's. having no crod flying around makes these very easy to use while cutting the lawn, on a train or just lounging around the house.

Pairing - I had no issues pairing this to my Iphone 5S. Following the included instaruction, I was up and running within a minute or so.

Battery life - This is one area that I am hoping I will see improvements. The first 2 charges have not lasted very long. I have gotten about 6 hours per charge so far and I believe these are supposed to last more like 12. I know some batteries improve with a few uses so I am hoping that is the case here. Or it is possible that the rated battery life is based on lower volumes or something. I tend to listen loud so maybe that is killing my battery.

Sound - These headphones were a bit disappointing at first. Coming off the M50's and having my ears trained to hear those, I found these headphones a bit flat and a bit too bass heavy at first. I tend to listen to music with no EQ with my M50's but I find I need to EQ these headphones a bit. I have been playing around with various settings (on Spotify) and find that a treble boost seems to take away some of the "muddy" lowe end sound. It is not perfect but it helps a lot. I think these are just designed to push the bass a bit more since people think that equals quality. As far as soundstage, I find these to be very up front with little soundstage. Great for heavy rock music that I listen to. However, I do get some separation at times wich makes them feel a bit more full. But not a wide soundsatage by any means. If you are listebing to orchestra type music, I would try these before you buy to make sure they work well for that environment.

Cord vs Cordless - the great news so far is that I haven't heard any difference between the two with quality of the music. Running cordless, these are LOUD headphones with my 5S. I am running them at about 75% volume which is in line with my M50's. I find they run the same with the cord. I have had no dropped sound running wireless. These just work well.

Overall these are going to be with me for the near term. I love the fact that I am no longer restricted by a cord to get great sound. I can live with the need to EQ to deal with the low end issue (although this does not work with amazon music) . These are definitley worth considering if you are in the market for quality cordless headphones

review_text:
Solid Wireless Headphone. This won't be a full review yet because I just got my pair a couple of days ago from V-Moda, but so far they are awesome.(edit. week and a half in now and still really liking these.)

Coming from using the M100 religiously, they sound equal to actually significantly better in some areas.

The M100 is great for bass while keeping everything else crystal clear. The Crossfade Wireless seems to improve on the mid clarity while tightening up the bass and keepin it punchy.
This goes for wired and wireless and I honestly can barely tell a difference in sound quality between wired and wireless.

The construction is very much like the M100 and I used my XL ear pads on the wireless. I opted for the gunmetal version and although mines has a blue tint to them I still really like them, they just seem different that I expected.

The pairing was easy enough and I know for my iPhone 6, that the notifications screen shows the battery percentage while the main screen shows a new battery bar by the phones battery bar that shows how much juice the Crossfade Wireless has left in it. I have used them wirelessly for around 5 hours so far and it shows about 60% battery left.

The controls feel good and seem sturdy and reliable. They work a lot like the three button remotes on apple headphones.

I really like that there is a wired mode that immediately shuts down wireless mode as soon as you plug it into a 3.5mm jack. This turns off the battery and allows for unlimited listening in wired mode whereas some wireless headphones always need the battery to be used.

My only issue comes from the M100. Cliqfold and the lack of it. The M100 came with an awesome feature called cliqfold that allowed the headphones to fold up really nice and compact. That feature seems to have been omitted here and I don't see a logical reason why just yet. They are still very portable so I didn't feel it enough to dock a star for.

Overall they are great wireless headphones from a company that initially never seemed like they would make wireless headphones. I feel a lot of time went into tuning and although my experience with wireless Bluetooth headphones is limited, I know these are the best I've heard. These are easy to recommend and I'll keep updating my review as I have more time with them.

Now using these for about a week and a half now, everything has held up. The battery life listening at roughly 50%-75% gets me right around 12 hours. Connectivity is typically fast and responsive and now using it to make calls, microphone clarity is good with moderate background noise and great in quieter settings.

I wanted to point out that for those who are not familiar with the V-Moda headphones, these are not audiophile headphones in the standard sense. These are not neutral headphones. In my opinion they work pretty great for every kind of music you can throw at it but they are tuned for modern music, rock, rap, hip hop, electronic, and so on. The bass is forward and punchy yet clean which takes slightly away from the mid but still sounds fairly clean. The highs are forward but not harsh and overall there is a nice and very fun balance. These are easily the best bass geared headphones I have listened to based on leaving the mids and highs intact. The soundstage is reasonable for closed headphones and while it won't compete with any open air headphones, they aren't meant to. I have listened to rock, classic rock, hip hop, rap, EDM, country, and even classical music without any issues. While they are not my preferred method of listening to classical music, they do a great job considering what these headphones are geared towards.

UPDATE 1:
Forgot to mention that comfort for the Crossfade Wireless is similar to the M100. With the stock earcups comfort is good but after a few hours it is not great. I recommend the XL Earcups if you experience a good deal of discomfort after long term use. I do have a big head so try out the standard cups first but for me the XL earcups add a lot more comfort.

*This review is for the Gunmetal Version

Get these to show the loves of your life that you love them!!. Like HEAVEN on my ears. What a DELIGHT these headphones are. You can use them with bluetooth with a very easy pairing system (you just hold the button to the side to pair them!), and if you run out of battery power (or just want to simplify) you can also plug into the headphone jack with the included 24k gold plated cables. What an amazing package this is. It's truly a way to spoil someone that loves music, TV, games, etc. You can make and take calls with it!! There's a hidden mic that is CRYSTAL clear. Yesterday I was playing a game on my phone on bluetooth and it interupted me to take a call, then went right back to the game. It's so intuitive. I mean really they are just plain SEXY.

There's a special warranty that comes with these headphones, and a hard case so that they don't get damaged. You can even order custom-printed guards on the outside - that you can design to be 3D printed, starting at $40 and going all the way up to $500 for pure gold!!

If you have someone in your life that deserves some serious spoiling, get these headphones. They will have these for LIFE. The sound is amazing. The parts are all replaceable if they need to be (although I've had a more simple pair of them for over 5 years now and they are still as good as new!).

review_text:
I'm in love with these headphones. Comfortable for hours, amazing sound quality, beautifully made. I'm in love with these headphones. I'm a huge headphone nerd and have probably a dozen pairs of varying styles and brands -- I have an old pair of M100 Crossfades that've served me well, and the new wireless option caught my attention.

V-MODA over-the-hear Crossfades are a huge win: they look beautiful, with quality craftsmanship and design, and sound even better. The slick design is comfortable for hours of wear - usually 6-8/day for me - without any issues. They aren't isolating or active sound-blocking, but the enclosed memory foam earcup keeps sound from leaking and lets me enjoy my music without having to crank it up.

Bass kicks without drowning out mids; trebels are tight and sound great without being flat or tinny. The sound quality between wired and Bluetooth is essentially the exact same - a relief, given some BT headphones are kind of lossy.

The wired/wireless dual option is so convenient: the included cable is thoughtfully and well-designed, too, making it prepared for any and all uses without fraying or falling apart. The cable also has controls for volume built-in, which is handy when your phone or iPod is in your bag/pocket. The battery life is at least ten hours over BlueTooth, and it's a godsend when I'm working or at the gym. Pairing is quick and painless, taking just a second.

review_text:
A quality experience from arrival to the day that they will eventually be taken off my head. This is my first foray into the world of V-Moda and from the first moment I took them out of the box my inner voice said, "What took you so long" referencing my reluctance to take the plunge to try them.

My first impression was how light they are. One would expect these things to weigh a ton (which I think was my original resistance) but they are actually light and feel very balanced. They, in a word are awe-inspiring just to look at in the package. V-Moda seems to pride themselves on the presentation and getting the message across that "We don't just look good, we act good" which is regards to their warranty and service dialogues.

My nephew (a gamer) made almost identical noises as he did when he saw the most recent Star Wars trailer when he saw the empty V-Moda box on the table. A reaction that also let me know that the V-Moda marketing works! But let's take a listen.

The headset is comfortable with a soft by firm squeeze to my head. Pairing was a cinch (iPhone6) and sound was pretty remarkable just listening to mp3's on my phone. review_text:
I'm in love with these headphones. Comfortable for hours, amazing sound quality, beautifully made. I'm in love with these headphones. I'm a huge headphone nerd and have probably a dozen pairs of varying styles and brands -- I have an old pair of M100 Crossfades that've served me well, and the new wireless option caught my attention.

V-MODA over-the-hear Crossfades are a huge win: they look beautiful, with quality craftsmanship and design, and sound even better. The slick design is comfortable for hours of wear - usually 6-8/day for me - without any issues. They aren't isolating or active sound-blocking, but the enclosed memory foam earcup keeps sound from leaking and lets me enjoy my music without having to crank it up.

Bass kicks without drowning out mids; trebels are tight and sound great without being flat or tinny. The sound quality between wired and Bluetooth is essentially the exact same - a relief, given some BT headphones are kind of lossy.

The wired/wireless dual option is so convenient: the included cable is thoughtfully and well-designed, too, making it prepared for any and all uses without fraying or falling apart. The cable also has controls for volume built-in, which is handy when your phone or iPod is in your bag/pocket. The battery life is at least ten hours over BlueTooth, and it's a godsend when I'm working or at the gym. Pairing is quick and painless, taking just a second.

review_text:
A Fantastic Wireless Headphone.. Got my Crossfade Wireless today in gunmetal. I threw on my steel 3D printed V-MODA plates, the XL Pads and I'm a happy camper (not a big fan of the shiny gunmetal stock shields). These headphones are incredible. Side by side comparisons are virtually identical to the M100 in wired mode and outside of a little bit of clipping at high volume via bluetooth, the audio quality is still fantastic in wireless mode. I really could not be happier w/ these things. Compared to something like the Beats Studio Wireless, the V-MODAS easily win as they don't have the noise cancelling hiss the Studios do. That irritates me and with as little travel as I do, noise cancelling is not necessary.

One thing to note, the steel shields are also a bit on the heavy side compared to the stock aluminum but they look fantastic IMO so the tradeoff is worth it. This is a fantastic addition to the Crossfade lineup. Oh how I wish they had Click Fold hinges though like the M100. Maybe in the next version.

Either way, kudos to V-MODA for another great headphone.

review_text:
Probably the best bluetooth headphones out there so far, but not perfect yet. To be completely honest here, I'm a pretty big V-Moda fan when it comes to their crossfade line. I've owned the LP, the LP2, the M-100, and now these. I've had the chance to see just what V-Moda can do with their sounds.

The crossfade wireless is advertised, more or less, an M-100 with bluetooth and re-tuned drivers. Unfortunately, the only thing it truly retains from the M-100 is the way it looks.

Looking at the outside of the headphones, they're the same beautiful V-Moda crossfades that we've seen throughout their line--with buttons. The buttons look nice. They aren't obtrusive and they don't make you stand out like a lighthouse should you walk around with these in the middle of the night. The only light on the headphone is a fairly dim power light on the power switch. With that being said, I dislike the buttons. On the bottom of the headphone, we have the switch. Nothing wrong here, very sturdy feel to it. But at the top, we have the three buttons we will be using the most--Multi-Function (Play/Pause/Command), Volume up, and volume down. These three buttons feel flimsy to me and for worse, they are kind of hard to press, for some reason presenting resistance particularly when I try to turn the volume down. Perhaps they made it this way to avoid accidental pressing, but these buttons are right underneath the metal clip that holds the band to the cans so I'd imagine it would be somewhat difficult to bump into something that would hit the buttons here.

On the inside, we have a whole new story. If you're coming from the M-100, these are supposed to sound the same. Even after burn-in, the sound felt almost hollow to me, compared to the M-100. The bass was lacking, both on bluetooth and wireless, which is what most seem to buy V-Modas for. The mids were recessed, but this is no change from the M-100. The highs were also present, so no change here. Somewhere along the line, V-Moda tweaked these headphones and dropped (upped?) the bass from the M-100s. These headphones also lack aptX lossless/low-latency codec which is a major disappointment in this price range. The Sony MDR10BT has it and costs less. What gives, V-Moda?

The other thing to note in regards to the bluetooth is that if you listen to softer music, you may notice a near-silent static playing along with your music. This seems to be the standard for bluetooth headphones.

Other notes:
- The micro USB charging port is on the LEFT cup, while the 3.5mm plug is on the RIGHT cup. I prefer my wire on the left side, so this is entirely up to user preference.
- These lose the cliquefold mechanism that was so popular with the M-100. Bluetooth is intended for mobility, so it's strange that this would get removed, but it may be a design limitation here. If you're coming from the M-100, expect the larger LP case.
- These can be paired and connected with more than one device at a time, but can only play one at a time. This is pretty interesting, since the M-100s had two ports so that you could either listen to two sources at once or daisy chain your headphones. Unfortunately you can not stream to the cans and use the 3.5mm port as an audio-out.
- If you have the M-100s, or really any headphones that have a removable audio-in cable and want wireless, I'd check out these: [[ASIN:B0134DTP9Q BTunes VXB-35 (3.5mm Model) To Make Wired Headphones Wireless for Beats, Monster, Sony, V-Moda, Marshalls and more]]. I'm ended up returning my Crossfade Wireless and buying this instead.

review_text:
Love these!!. I already had a couple of V-Moda headphones [[ASIN:B00GO4GMHQ V-MODA XS On-Ear Folding Design Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone (White Silver)]] and [[ASIN:B003BYRGKE V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone (Rouge)]] both of which I have been satisfied with, but honestly I haven't been using them that much lately because they were not wireless and when I go to the gym or listen to music before I go to sleep, the wire just got in the way. Luckily I also had the [[ASIN:B00KGGK71A Samsung Level Over-Ear Bluetooth Headphone - Retail Packaging - Black]] which are an excellent set of headphones that I used in the gym as well as occasionally before I go to sleep. The downside to these otherwise great headphones is that they are huge and tend to get hot with prolonged use. I attempted to use the Bluetooth adapter with my wired VModa headphones, but they were too tacky and too cumbersome to use.

Introducing the WIRELESS V-Moda Crossfade over the head headphones!!! In short these headphones are excellent in almost every way. They combine the great sound from my wired V-Moda headphones with the convenience of wireless capability of my Samsung level over set. Comparing these with the Samsungs which sound excellent I would say these sound slightly better with a little deeper bass and fuller sound. A big advantage of these over the Samsungs is that they are more comfortable to wear. They do not get hot and because they are so light weight I can wear them for an extended period of time without them being uncomfortable. They also look great and offer customizable choices of ear plates ranging from $20 to well over $400 for the precious metal options.

Connecting these to your Bluetooth enabled devices is a snap, just set follow the easy to read instructions included in the packaging and you'll be connected to your phone, tablet, or music device in seconds. Another great option (which are also on the Samsungs) is if your battery is low or don't want to use Bluetooth, then you can plug in a standard earphone wire (included) into the side and these immediately turn into a wired set of headphones. This is also convenient for gaming because while they are wireless, my PS4 does not recognize these headphones when trying to connect them to my console via Bluetooth. I wish I could use the wireless option for my PS4, but that is not the fault of these headphones.

These headphones have many of the same features as the Samsungs, but there is one thing the Samsungs do a little better. On the Level Overs, volume control and track skipping are controlled by a integrated touch pad embedded in the right earpiece. So simply running your finger up over the side of these headphones would instantly turn the volume up, and running your finger down, will turn the volume down. Track skipping/backtracking is controlled by forward and backwards motions with your finger. To pause you just simply tap your finger and to resume tap your finger again. While the V-Moda can do the same thing, these functions are controlled by physical buttons. There are two buttons for volume up and volume down, and a single button that controls track skipping as well as pausing/resuming. To pause just tap the button once, to skip to the next track tap the button twice, but your timing has to be just right or it will just pause the song. In addition there doesn't seem to be a way to go back to the previous track.

Other than the downside I mentioned these are excellent high quality comfortable headphones that should leave you satisfied for a long time.

review_text:
Excellent!. I will jump straight to the point. Please keep in mind that I am not an audiophile, but do pursue better quality audio products where it matters.

* Size, Weight, Packaging: These full size over-the-ear headphones have moderate weight, a bit on the heavy side comparing to regular headphones but not much different from the weight of noise-cancelling or wireless over-the-ear phones. They are not portable and come with a custom-molded very nice black hard case with a zipper. Two cables are included: male-male 3.5" audio cable and a flat micro-USB cable for charging, as well as an RCA Y-to-3.5" adapter and a small instruction booklet.

* Comfort: The headband is a bit tight, but this keeps the phones tightly and securely positioned on your head. Absolutely no wobbling! The leather (or leather-like -- I am not sure exactly) material of covering the headband and ear cushions is nice and soft. It feels a bit hot around the ears after wearing them for about 1 hour, but not too uncomfortable.

* Sound Quality: I am more than satisfied with the range and the quality of the highs and lows. The sound feels "just right" -- very comfortably soft, not too high or crackling and not too low to the point of being boomy.

* Operation: The headphones hold the charge very well. To turn the power on and off, you will need to slide a switch, which is easy to slide with one finger. The power button is inconspicuously located on the outer side (not along the perimeter, as in some headphones), so it takes getting used to finding it by touch. review_text:
I've got no strings on me!. I love running with over-ear headphones, and lately my Crossfade M-100s have been my go-to cans for that. The one thing that I've always hated while running with any headphones is dealing with the cords - pulling earbuds out of my ears, rubbing and getting in the way of arm movement with on-ear or over-ear, etc. I can tuck them in my shirt or whatever, but then they're annoying and pull when I turn my head. And let's be honest - most cordless headphones sound like garbage. Been there, done that, returned it. Yeah, first world problems but why not shoot for perfection? The only reason I even gave these a shot is because they're V-MODA and I'm not just surprised, I'm blown away.

V-MODA claims that these sound equivalent to wired headphones. I'm going to disagree for my most common use case - connected directly to my iPhone 6S. In this case, they sound a bit better. The integrated amplified delivers more and cleaner bass presence than my iPhone can. Not as good as with a standalone DAC/amp, but I'd say about 30% better than the iPhone alone - which is not a subtle improvement, and without the distortions introduced by the iPhone's electronic equalizer. You can practically see the strings on a bass guitar vibrating in your mind, and the bass drums have a beautiful kick. Highs and mids still feature V-MODA's trademark clarity and nice, even frequency response. So yes, the sound is wonderful, which is what everyone really cares about. I've seen some complaints in forums, but as far as I can tell these have been narrowed down to devices that just can't send good quality audio over Bluetooth. I haven't personally had any issues yet, but I've only tested with my iPhone and MacBook Pro. Charging is accomplished with a standard micro-USB cable, so most people won't have to worry about carrying extra cords or chargers to keep the Crossfade Wireless topped up while traveling. Battery life hasn't yet been an issue. They come with a typically excellent V-MODA travel case, the sort that puts every other brand to shame but V-MODA buyers have become pleasantly used to.

Minor quibbles:
* No cliq-fold hinges like the M-100s and XS. Sorry, V-MODA, you spoiled us and it's hard to go back.
* A single button for pause / resume / track-forward / track-back. I suck at pressing these fast enough, so I always wind up just pausing it.

I'm pretty nit-picky about things, so that's a pretty short list. I'm loving these so far!

negative_points: Lacks cliq-fold hinges
Single control button is difficult to use for multiple functions like track navigation
positive_points: Delivers more and cleaner bass presence when connected to an iPhone 6S
Highs and mids feature trademark clarity and even frequency response
Uses a standard micro-USB cable for charging
customer_issues: Difficulty pressing the single control button fast enough for track-forward or track-back functions

aspect_sentiments.evidence: Charging is accomplished with a standard micro-USB cable
Battery life hasn't yet been an issue
A single button for pause / resume / track-forward / track-back

result.review_summary: The customer is highly satisfied with the wireless headphones, praising their sound quality, micro-USB charging, and travel case, while noting minor drawbacks regarding the hinges and single control button.

review_text:
Awesome SQ; the fact that it's wireless in icing on the cake!. Just recently received the V-MODA Crossfade Wireless and I got to say, I think the team at V-MODA hit this one out of the park. Just a little on my background -- I have owned the M-80 (which I have since gifted), and I own the XS as well as the M-100 so I have a sense of the V-MODA house sound. I also have owned a bunch of other portable headphones (you can check my profile to see which ones), mostly because I appreciate a lot of different sound signatures and certain unique characteristics of each headphone I own. Which could also mean I can't make up my mind lol but I love them all for different reasons and wish I could just be the one-headphone kind of person but alas, I cannot. I also listen to all genres, mainly rock/alternative. I listen to most of my music on-the-go, being that I live in NYC and I am always on the move. So portability, great sound quality, and isolation are all paramount. I also appreciate style and comfort but not as much as SQ.

For a long time, I would be skeptical about BT headphones. Although every once in a while I'd see someone with a set of BT cans from well-known companies, and I'd think there must be a certain kind of liberty I am missing out on, not having to deal with cables. I thought to myself, I would love to try that and have that freedom on the go. But like I said SQ, is above and beyond, necessary for me as now my ears have been spoiled by good SQ. I don't claim to be an expert and don't have 'golden ears'. But I do go by what I hear and how I feel hearing it. And I'd like to think that I know what crappy, murky sound, sounds like. On that note..

I know I might be hyping these up, but I really really dig these cans and feel like they might be the ultimate portable solution for me. Because of the convenience of no cables as well as the awesome SQ, I am afraid it may make all my other cans a bit.. obsolete. Only time will tell and there are some cans that I own that are staples in collection but some others could be on their way out soon (as I would hope to simplify and thin out the herd at some point) I do love different sound signatures and different characteristics that headphones have to offer this CFW takes the cake for my needs. To my ears, they are detailed, warm, pleasant, lively and enjoyable on the move or even at home. They are on the warm side and the low end boasts a full bodied beautiful clean bass. Compared to the M-100 I feel the CFW sounds a bit cleaner across the spectrum TBH. In wireless mode, they are very very similar, almost identical. In wired mode, it is slightly more improved with tighter bass and airier highs. Otherwise not a huge difference to the point where I would want to use these in wired mode. They sound too good in wireless mode! It's great however that they sound so good in wired mode, and that I have the option to use them and know I'm getting great SQ whenever the battery runs out, on the go. So being that I had been thinking about getting a BT headphone for a while but concerned about SQ and also any possible BT technology malfunctions that I read were happening with other cans recently, I was intrigued upon learning that V-MODA was coming out with a wireless headphone and keeping tabs on it. Count me a fan of the V-MODA house sound (as well as the beautiful aesthetics and BQ) and I was just hoping that the SQ was going to be up to snuff. I am happy to say that the CFW exceeded my expectations.

So let's get into the sound:

Bass: The bass hits hard with plenty of impact, remains tight, and reaches deep. I have a deep appreciation for lower sub bass detail and can't stand anything that has that one-note bass. Anyone who has heard the M-100 knows how deep it reaches and these deliver all the same. It's definitely north of neutral but there is plenty of detail and texture, and for portable applications, it's the perfect amount of bass as the low end is the first part of the frequency to go when in a loud environment. The lows give the overall sound plenty of body and warmth, without sounding slow at the least. Good sense of PRaT and energy as well. Very tight and clean IMHO.

Mids: The mids align nicely with the rest of the spectrum. They are not in your face or pushed forward in any way, but they're not recessed in the least. To my ears, this is great because if the mids were any more forward they would be fatiguing, yet I don't feel like I am missing out on the detail with instruments and vocals at all. Male vocals sound deep and smooth and female vocals sound very natural and not overly bright. There is a great clarity and instruments have a nice sense of decay without ever sounding slow. Very smooth and natural-sounding overall. Feels like you're in the orchestra-section at a concert.

Highs: The highs are sparkly without harshness! They are smooth but not overly smooth and nicely extended. This is a great feat because you have to have some sparkle for high hats, trumpets, and brush strokes to sound accurate with the right timbre. At the same time, especially when if I am in a loud setting and want to increase the volume by a notch or so, these haven't fatigued my ears with the treble. Nice and smooth yet sparkly.

Soundstage and imaging: I would say soundstage and imaging are about average. Good width and height. The M-100 sounds slightly deeper in comparison but for me, made things sound a little too far away. I like that these sound a bit more intimate yet still having the out-of-your-head experience. While the M-100 sounds like a deep hall, I'd say these sound like a deep and wide chamber orchestra room. Sounds like I'm at an intimate, unplugged (no pun intended) jam session with my favorite band. It's a delight to my ears, warm and sweet.

Isolation: Isolation is about average, not bad for a circumaural portable, better than the XS, not as good as my HD25 or DT-1350 which isolate a bit more.

If I could characterize these headphones in a few words, I would say they are musical, detailed, euphonic, natural with a "fun" sound that any audiophile can enjoy. These, being wireless is incredible icing on the cake, as that is never at the expense of SQ to my ears. I have these on my head and still can't believe I am not connected to my DAP by a wire (using these with my iPhone 6 listening to ALAC and Spotify). They are highly convenient and if my fiancee doesn't permanently kidnap these from me, I can see myself using this headphone as my predominant headphone, only using the others that I have in case I miss a certain headphone's sonic sig/characteristics.

This is my first BT headphone so I'm happy to see how easy and intuitive it's been to use. Also the buttons are well-placed while being nicely discreet. I love that there is no obvious, bright blue flashing light that tells the world this is a BT can. The small v-light that lights up on the bottom is nice and discreet. So far so good with the BT connection to my phone. I haven't heard any clipping or anything. I am very impressed. It appears V-MODA has taken a lot of time testing these out, which I expect no less. Build quality is great. Battery life is also great, I have only charged these once when I received them in the last few days (about a couple of hours a day) and they still have a full charge. I know some people which that these had the clip-fold but frankly I am quite ok with it. This way I am a little more ginger with these cans -- I tend to be rough with the M-100 when I would fold them up throw them in my bag. I would rather less moving parts and so far they have been quite the travel buddy. The M-100 will be my beater, slightly more portable back-up.

Lastly, these are at an amazing price-point. Glad that V-MODA did not boost up the price to way more because of its BT capabilities, like a lot of other companies have. I think for anyone who have come to appreciate the V-MODA house sound with the M-100 and XS, these are a no-brainer. Plus it's great to know that V-MODA always has your back in case there is a problem with your gear and has outstanding warranty and customer service. All in all, I am a happy camper and these will be a permanent staple in my stable of cans. Happy listening and thanks for reading!

Full bodied beautiful clean bass with plenty of detail

A refined M-100 with wireless capabilities? Oh yes!. V-Moda is a brand that has always been very fashion forward. It was until the M80 and M100 in which they were able take traction and gain popularity by merging their designs with respectable acoustics that was generally pleasing to a wide range of people. Now, they have finally taken what made them popular and removed the wires. This is the new Crossfade Wireless.

The box is a bit taller than the M100’s version because there is no longer the click fold hinge that allowed the headphone to collapse in upon self, rendering the new Crossfade wireless not as portable. This may be a deal breaker to some, but the included case is still of quality and attempts to minimize its footprint by molding its shape to the headphone. Included in the box is a spare set of shields usually this will be the custom set you’ve created. You have your quick guide and warranty information especially informing you about V-Moda’s kick ass immortal life program. Inside the specially molded clamshell zipper case you’ll find the micro USB cable to charge your headphones and the 1 button with an in-line microphone cable allowing you to use the Crossfade wireless in passive mode in the event the battery dies or you simply yearn for the best possibly sound quality. And at last you have the clip to mount the case on a bag or your belt.

The Crossfade Wireless retains the same incredibly rugged and sexy design as the M-100 and LP series. What’s even more amazing is that it keeps the same size even despite now housing internal electronics to allow wireless connectivity. I have the XL pads installed and these offer improved cushion depth, a bigger soundstage and a smoother sound as well a wider ear diameter for superior comfort over the stock pads. A much recommended upgrade. The headband offers substantial padding to avoid hot points at the top of the head and remains aesthetically pleasing by not being overly bulky and/or not aligning to the curvature of your head. In summary, these are gorgeous, well-built headphones that can easily withstand everyday wear and tear and if you do break them, the immortal life program is an option.
The location of the wireless controls are fairly intuitive. On the top left we have the volume down button. On the top middle, we have the multi button, play, pause, answer and reject calls as well as activating your voice assistant and on the top right we have the volume up button. Moving down we have a single rocker that when pushed to the middle turns on the headphone and pairs it to the last known device and when pushed and held to the far right for 2-3 seconds puts it in pairing mode. The Crossfade wireless can be connected to 2 devices at once, for example a smart watch and a smart phone or a smart phone and a tablet.

The M-100 was at a time my favorite headphone, but it was until I ventured off into what other high quality portable offerings were available that made me see its flaws. The M-100 is undeniably a pleasing and fun sounding headphone with stunning bass performance, but its resolution and coherency leaved some to be desired. The Crossfade Wireless is a welcoming improvement. By taking the famous M-100 sound and fine tuning the frequency response balance to be more linear as well as brining out more resolving power to allow the subtle textures and harmonic low level details to surface has resulted in being my favorite Bluetooth headphone, period and possibly being my overall “favorite” sounding headphone surpassing the Master & Dynamic MH40. Yes, these are that DAMN good. When in Bluetooth operation, the following said about the sound quality of the Crossfade Wireless is still mostly the same, but it just doesn’t have the same level of detail and overall focus as when it is wired and plugged into a fine setup. Other than that, these are the best sounding Bluetooth headphones I have heard and owned surpassing the Parrot Zik 2, Sennheiser Momentum Wireless, Sony XB950BT, Bang & Olufsen H8, Definitive Technology Symphony 1, Beats Studio Wireless, Beats Solo2 Wireless, Samsung Level Over and Bowers & Wilkins P5 Wireless. The sound of Crossfade wireless is still immediately on the fun sounding side of the spectrum, but still very refined and coherent. No part of the frequency range is absent.

The bass extends endlessly and punches you with no mercy when the song calls for it. This is one of the most downright seductive bass presentations that I have ever heard and it manages to integrate into the midrange quite stupendously well without destroying that whole octave. The midrange is still a bit relaxed, but it’s more neutral sounding than the M100 and sounds clean and proportionally well represented. Vocals sound rich and full even whilst the bass is turning the skin on your face into water waves. The treble seems a bit more present and extended over the M100, but most importantly, it’s a cleaner and more natural sounding treble which really helps clean up the initial transients thus improving imaging and granting the Crossfade Wireless a very, very good soundstage for a closed back and among my best performers in that region.

Now, these aren’t my best sounding portables, but they are not far from it whilst retaining a character that grants them undeniable enjoy ability. I love to be able hear every single thing in the recording, but I more importantly enjoy feeling the emotion in the recording more and this is where the Crossfade Wireless excels.

Bluetooth operation does not have the same level of detail as wired operation
