These Sound Great, but the Fit is Tight. I do not consider myself an audiophile, but I can discern different qualities of headphones. I typically wear earbuds, which are my preference. With that said, these Crossfade Wireless over the ear headphones have a very good sound quality to them. I dare say that they are excellent.

If you prefer bass in your music, then these are the right headphones for you. These earphones seem to trend toward the bassier side of things.

Generally, I don't like over the ear headphones because others can hear what I am listening to. When I'm in an office environment, this can be an issue because I play my music loud. The sound leaks out of the earcups. This is nothing new, as I have experienced that with other brands as well.

I found these to be quite tight on my head, which after a while is something I could adjust to. They certainly won't be sliding off due to rapid head movements.

I was excited to try these immediately after unboxing them, so I skipped charging the battery (for use with Bluetooth) and went straight to plugging in the included cable. These work fine as wired headphones.

Overall, these are great sounding headphones, that can be wired or wireless, depending on your choice or patience (or lack thereof).

review_text:
Nearly Perfect. Nearly the perfect headphone. With the XL pads I bought it's extremely comfy, sounds great, 12 hours is a good playtime amount, very sturdy, excellent warranty, free shield from ordering at vmoda.com, the list goes on and on.

Why the 4 stars?

It's a small gripe from me but it's big enough of an issue for me to not want to give this headphone a 5 star.

When you connect the device and it plays the startup/connection audio, or any time it stops playing audio either when you pause the music/end the video or there's a small period of silence, you will hear a distinct and somewhat loud static in the background for about a second while the headphones wait for potential new audio, then they fully go into quiet standby mode after that second of static. I know there's probably nothing that can be done about this because that's just how wireless headphones are, but it's still annoying to hear nonetheless as I do sometimes either pause my songs or after I finish watching a Youtube video I can hear it for that second.

Don't at all let this detract you from wanting this headphone, once the audio starts playing and while it's playing it sounds awesome, and like I said in the first sentence of the review it's an amazing pair of headphones and I'll never go to another brand, V-moda all the way for their sound, build quality, comfort, and service.

review_text:
Boom Boom Pow!. I have owned/purchased several different types of headphones in the past ….Beats, Koss, Sony, Sennheiser, even wired V-moda’s, and I would say these are in my top two.

These headphones are attractive..I received these in gunmetal black. If you’d like to customize your look, you can order different colored metal shields and ear cushions.

The earmuffs have soft cushions and surround the entire ear. More importantly, these muffs allow for several hours of comfort if worn for extended periods of time. The volume control and mic are integrated on the right side of the headset. And while these can be worn for several activities, I wouldn’t really suggest working out in them, they are too nice (or expensive), but it can be done.

The headset comes with their own case, a USB charging cord, a 3.5mm 45’ degree plug with 24k gold tips and a clip to hang them from your bag or jeans. Bluetooth connection is fairly easy, there is a switch that you push on the back of the right earpiece. Once activated it gives a tone that lets you know it is trying to connect. Once you activate bluetooth on your device, it is ready.That’s right, these headphones provide great sound and are WIRELESS. What a fantastic feature. And you even have the option of not using the wireless feature by connecting to various portable devices (i.e., smartphone, laptop, tablets, etc) with the provided “mic 1 speakeasy cable”.

And finally, when I listened to different genres of music (i.e., jazz, rock, rap, classical) , the sound was clear and the quality is among the best. The frequency response listed is 5Hz-30kHz and that appears to be accurate. The sound wasn’t muted or distorted.

Overall, I would give these headsets 5 stars. These are definitely worth the money.

review_text:
Sadly, I returned them.. These sound absolutely phenomenal. You can "feel" the bass. The mids and highs are great too. Also, the volume or amp is very strong and loud enough. In short, they (almost) sound wired.

Unfortunately, I returned them. My primary reason is b/c they were uncomfortable, even with the XL pads. A quality, denser memory foam, stitched in leather would probably cure the comfort issue. Also, a swivel headband or swivel ear-cups would aid in comfort as well.

Other notable concerns: 1) Calls weren't clear 2) There isn't a battery life indicator. 3) Sound leakage is too easy for others to hear what you're listening to. 4) Ear-cups don't fold or collapse into the headband. 5) "V" shaped ear-cups detract from the fit. Ear shaped cups would probably capture the outer ears better. 6) The "buttons" on the headset were hard to detect. I couldn't get a feel for the on, off or volume buttons.

review_text:
Best headphones for video editing and relaxing!. I am a video editor and need great sounding headphones for audio mixing. I need to be able to hear the lowest of the lows along with the highest of the highs and everything in between. To get right to it, I have absolutely nothing bad to say about these headphones. I used to own a pair of the m-100's and decided to try the wireless after reading many reviews about how great these headphones were. I also have cats at home that tend to chew on and destroy cords, so I decided to hunt down the best sounding wireless headphones.

One thing I am kind of sad about is that they don't retract like the m-100's do but it actually worked out better for me because the case stays strapped onto my backpack better with the bigger case. I have yet to experience any lag with the audio. The transition from going between wireless and wired is seamless, the is no break in the audio playback if you need to plug in and charge them. It was a little confusing trying to connect my the headphones to my iMac at work because I also have bluetooth desktop speakers, I realized that those had to be unpaired and completely disconnected before I could pair my v-moda's, then I could pair the other speakers. I switch between using headphones and speakers often to show the producer what I've been working on. After the initial pairing, they just connect when you turn them on, easy peasy. The battery life lasts quite a long time, a couple days of video editing for me. The sound quality is just perfect. They are super comfortable and durable. I'm not afraid to take these on a film set to record audio. I can hear every little detail when listening to music or when I'm mixing audio. I also use the FiiO portable amp with my phone when I want a little more rumble in the bass.

Ok actually there may be one thing that I noticed when I was charging them via USB through my computer, I also had them plugged into the same computer so I could keep editing but I got some static and that I couldn't work with, so as a work around, I plugged them into an outlet nearby so they could continue charging as I was editing and the static went away. So for that I would give these headphones a 9 out of 10 score but still a 5 out of 5 stars.

If you're looking for stylish, great sounding headphones for listening to music or mixing audio or both, I recommend the V-MODA Wireless 100%!

review_text:
A closed back headphone that does well, surprised!. As someone who has other headphones such as HD700 and AKG K712 the new addition to the family, M100 Wireless is a pretty decent one, nothing spectacular but why does it get 5 stars?

First, M100 is a closed back headphone and its not like audiophile headphones which are all open back, so in terms of what it does with a closed back, it gets 5.

Design: pretty good actually, sturdy and metallic. If you are one of those who likes form over function then go get one but if you prefer music quality and want to sit down and listen to music for a sessions then visit audiophile forums such as head-fi.org etc.

The sound: Once you get used to wider sound stage, its hard very had to like anything else so m100 is a-o-k to me, now remember, I am saying this from the perspective of open back headphones but for anyone else, specially for those who never had a quality headphone, this will be mind blowing experience. Lows, mids and highs are not all over powering each other. I tested few edm tracks with vocals, and they do amazing. I probably used it about 20 hours and so far its hasn't caused any frequency issues.

Comfort: I did change to XL pad, which gave a deeper and wider sound stage and much more comfort than the original. I recommend the change asap. The original gave my ears lobes some pain, it didn't go around the ear completely and felt too tight. The headband might needs to be stretched out to loosen it a bit. Again, comfort is nothing like the two other headphones I listed, they are miles ahead in comfort.

Bluetooth: Again, I do not recommend using it as it lowers quality of sound. I did notice the drop and just use wired, or maybe my source, note 4.

Last note, I am using this with fiio-e6 portable amp, do you need one? No. Over all, you won't be disappointed, I like mine for what it is, a closed back headphone that does pretty damn good, surprised!

review_text:
After the long wait.. They are everything I expected!. Let me start off by saying that my first pair of V-Moda headphones were the [[ASIN:B003BYRGKY V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-the-Ear Headphones (Gunmetal Black)]]. I have had the LPs for a little over a year now with no complaints. These headphones were built like a tank and very bass heavy, which is what I was looking for. I was getting ready to purchase the M-100s then I saw these and with the reviews I had to get them. I ordered the Phantom Chrome from V-Moda's website so I was able to get a free pair of fiber custom shields!

Out of the box, the sounds is tremendously better than my LP's. They are about the same size and have about the same weight to them with the same tank like quality. The sound is crystal clear. I have Spotify with my music downloaded in high quality so I'm sure that helps these headphones get closer to their potential. You'll definitely want to upgrade your music quality to take advantage of what these headphones are capable of. However, from the reviews I read the bass isn't meeting expectations quite yet but neither did the LPs the first couple of days of use so I'm hoping the headphones will open up a bit after I break them in. Don't get me wrong though, these are one of the best headphones I've experienced.

If I had to complain about one thing, and this is with me being extremely picky, it would be about the weight of each side of the headphone. Coming from the LPs, I could tell that right side is a tad heavier than the left when sitting on my head due to the bluetooth technology on the right side. However, the longer they sit on your head the less you'll notice.

Overall these are great headphones and with V-Modas great immortal life program I can't see myself purchasing another pair of headphones. I'm not sure how long V-Moda will be offering the free set of custom fiber shields if you purchase from their website but if they are offering it that's what you should definitely do.

review_text:
"Superb Bluetooth" (two words I never thought would go into the same sentence). I've had these for a week and been alternating between them and their in-ear Zn model, and I'm in love with them both.

My experience with bluetooth has been limited insofar as I like music too much to use one of those crappy wireless speakers that came out over the past three years, and I tried the Bose Soundlink in 2013 when they first came out, but I couldn't tell if I didn't like the sound because of the bluetooth or because it was "a Bose"..

However, as I've had a set of V-MODA's bulletproof M-100s, and I know how good they sound, I figured that this would be a good apples-to-apples basis for comparison. All I can say is they got it right somehow.

First of all, I thought it would be a safe bet because if I didn't like the bluetooth (sound quality, pairing, battery life, etc.), I could always fall back to the included cable. But I've gone wireless for a week and I can't believe I have never once been tempted to abandon bluetooth for the cable. V-MODA's team pulled-off "superb bluetooth" (two words I never thought would go into the same sentence).

Secondly the control buttons respond really well. It took only 15 minutes for my hands to instinctively find them and with two quick taps I'm skipping songs here-and-there.

Congrats fellas!

review_text:
Review from someone that is NOT an audiophile. Just a lover of music, games and movies. Let's get this out of the way first - I am *not* an audiophile. I merely know when what I'm hearing sounds good or not. Long story short, these headphones sound GREAT. I'll break down what I use them with and how they performed:

Gaming - I own a PS4 and play a lot of Destiny, among other games. So like many I tried numerous gaming headsets. Sure, most of them are functional, but they're also almost all universally overpriced on top of only sounding average. So imagine my surprise when I plugged my new Crossfade Wireless into my Dualshock 4's headphone jack and it didn't suck. Not only didn't it suck, but it was actually quite great. I can only imagine how much better it would be if I had a mixamp connected to the optical out on the PS4 and plugged my Crossfades into that. Regardless, if you're getting these headphones to use on the controller, just know that it sounds exceptional. For those of you who are like me that need a microphone to talk to teammates, what I bought was the Boompro. It's also made by V-moda, and it's essentially just a wire that runs from your headphones to your controller and it has a great mic on it. The mic on it is better quality than any I used from Astro, Sony or Turtle Beach.

Music - I use these both in bluetooth or wired(whenever possible because wired sounds much better) on my Macbook and on my Android cellphone. My music sounds so good now. No matter how loud you make them, they never ever distort. The bass is very strong, but unlike the Beats Studio Wireless that I also tried before hearing about V-moda, the bass doesn't overpower everything else. I also tried the M50x headphones, and those are supposedly audiophile headphones, but I got so tired listening to music with them. They're so clear and the individual instruments so pronounced that I ended up focusing more on one thing than the entire arrangement. Everything sounds more cohesive on the Crossfade.

Movies - the main reason I went with the Crossfade Wireless over the V-Moda M100s is because I have an Apple TV 4 that doesn't have an optical out port, but it does support Bluetooth audio. I initially bought a pair of Beats Studio Wireless to watch movies/netflix etc wirelessly on the Apple TV but the audio wasn't very good and any time I hit rewind the headphones lost connection. On top of that the Studios were bad at music and gaming, and used battery even when in wired mode (how dumb is that? The Crossfades shut down all the electronics for Bluetooth when a wire is connected). Pairing was quick and easy and I was incredibly happy to hear that the audio quality was nearly as great wireless as it is wired. To test it out I watched Straight Outa Compton and Mad Max. Wow. You hear everything, and the bass is thundering when explosions etc go off.

On a side note, I had issues with the first pair I got. Amazon took them back and sent me another. The second pair appeared to be used and had numerous issues as well. Instead of dealing with Amazon again, I contacted V-Moda directly and they agreed to take a look and help me out. I sent the headphones to them and they then sent me a new pair. Their support team was great to me. Huge shout out to them (Richard and David). While I waited to have my headphones replaced, I went back to using a pair of Sony Wireless Gold. Talk about night and day. When my new Crossfades arrived the other day, I couldn't wait to start using them again and to stop using the Sony. Once you're used to hearing quality audio, nothing else can suffice. I even stopped watching movies until the new pair had arrived.

Other reviews bring it up, so I'll just concur with what they said - if you buy these headphones, but the XL ear pads. I think V-moda should suck it up and just stop putting the thinner ear pads on by default. Just put the XLs on all new headphones and sell the thin ones as an add-on. The thin ones hurt my ears/head tremendously. The XL pads do not. Eat the loss, V-moda, and start putting the XLs on all of them. You'll earn so much goodwill.

review_text:
One word fits this headphone; Superiority. To pure hearted minds of musical fanatics,
Many of you, I'm sure, are debating which set of headphones to get if you are reading this. I'm not an engineer and I don't know how this thing was made, but I can tell you one thing, V-Moda Wireless beats all the other headphones that I've purchased and returned in the last 12 months or so, in terms of quality of music.

I also prefer this over other headphones for other reasons as well.

So, Which ones am I talking about?
Beats solo2 wireless
Beats studio wireless
Sony Sony MDR-XB950BT/B(but this set is as good as beats or a bit superior in terms of sound quality
Sennheiser RS120

I find V-Moda wireless to be very sturdy. Of course, nothing is unbreakable but this seems to be sturdier than the ones above.

**Note
I also have wired BOSE Quiet Comfort 15(Limited edition) and WOW!!!
V-MODA Wireless beats the sound quality!!! Whatever type of music you are listening to, V-Moda wireless projects clearer sound and vocal pitch in EVERY WAY.

Plus, for those who workout, this is a very good set headphone to be listening to at the gym.

The price of Beats studio wireless is about the same as V-Moda Crossfade Wireless and you can't even compare these two.
Beats Studio Wireless is just full of hype, imo. It is not even worth getting it.

The only negative thing about this product is the COST. It is more expensive than the products I have mentioned above in a list, but if you prefer sound quality, durability and design over other factors, then this headphone is the way to go.

There is 1 year warranty on this product and if this product breakdown in any way or form so you can't use it, the company give you 50% off on the purchase of the same product. So you'll be paying $150 for this replacement after a year, assuming that the price doesn't change for this product.

Overall, I highly recommend this headphone.
I'm sorry if I don't sound very well worded. Hope you can use my review as a part of making your decision over spending 300 dollars headphone.

Just my 2 cents.

review_text:
Third time's a charm. edit 1/26/16: I couldn't resist the feeling like I gave up on them too soon so I ordered directly from v-moda a white crossfade wireless. I'm going through a second trial. Really loving them so far. Comparing them to my m100 the bass is definitely tighter and in bluetooth mode there's almost more bass. I really prefer the refinements of this sound wired or wireless to the original m100. I still love the m100, but those have gone to my wife and these are mine now. In my original review I mentioned some hiss/sizzle - it turns out these headphones are so clear that they make some recordings' flaws completely apparent. Yes, in low volume there is a bluetooth hiss, but at high volume what I was hearing on many tracks was hiss in the recording. I a/b this back and forth with the m100 and cfw in wired mode and the hiss was there at high volumes. Don't get me wrong, maxed out there might be hiss from the internal amp being pushed, but that's to be expected on any device with its volume maxed. I'm really enjoying them this time around, I have one more headphone to try out but its $550 from master and dynamic - and at that price point it better sound twice as good as these, because if it doesn't i'm sticking with v-moda. I'm leaving my old review up just for comparison's sake. Still leaving it at four stars because theres no 4.5 option. They make my temple and jaw sore after a while in normal use, and almost instantly when lying down. Also, I thougth cliq fold being omitted would be an issue but honestly the carrying case is form fitting and fits in my gym bag just as easily. Its not as short, but its flatter than the m100 case. Plus I found myself not folding my m100 because the earpads would get squished and began to flatten out prematurely. I had to order replacements.

The V-Moda Crossfade wireless is difficult for me to review because ultimately I returned it and kept the m100. The two I received had battle scars from shipping. Both were sealed with the vmoda red ribbon and had the stickers over the earcups so i'm presuming they were brand new. However the first one had scratches on the silver trim between the earcup and earpad. The replacement had a scuff on the earcup and the microphone had shifted in its housing. If you looked inside the pinhole you could see the mic warped to the left. I think there was insufficient packing material in the box and it was bouncing around. Thats not VModas fault. So none of this reflects my rating. Just letting people know to inspect their expensive new toys! Now for the rating.

I loved the wired sound, and really liked the wireless sound. Wired it is very reminiscent of the m100 with slightly tighter bass, and slightly less of it too. Its gives a sense of a more balanced sound than the m100. It is pretty much V-moda sound signature just refined slightly. If you don't A/B them you wouldn't know there's a difference.

Wireless was great unless you turned the volume on the headphone itself up past half, Then there would be this distortion/sizzle/hiss at the top end of the sound regardless of how low the volume was on the music player. Up past half, to me - is where the amp really drove the headphones and made the bass thump, but that's where the sizzle lived. It was hard for me to find a balance between player/headphone volume. The bluetooth was also not dead quiet. I don't listen to music very loudly so I could always hear the signal noise. Its not a "bluetooth" thing in the sense that not every device suffers from this, but I've encountered it before. I have a bluetooth dongle right next to me that doesn't have this line level hiss at all. This was my ultimate reason for not replacing it another time after the second dud. I got my m100 for half the cost of the CFW; I wasn't going to pay double when the main feature was not up to standard. I believe they are almost there. If there's a CFW 2.0 Val will probably address all the signal quality issues with bluetooth. Until then i'm sticking with wired m100.

Minor concerns of mine were the battery life over time (year two and up), sweat/rain damaging the electronics, and falls. The physical build quality is as durable as the m100 but the electronics add more variables that could fail in the event of a minor fall/spill. I know people use bluetooth on the go,so if you're on a train and they fall or it starts to rain, would the destruction be covered under warranty? Too scary for me to take that change.

so why 4 stars? They're excellent headphones wired, if you find the balance in volumes they're very good in wireless mode. I can be objective enough to know that something is good even though its not good for me in particular.

I got my m100 for half the cost of the CFW; I wasn't going to pay double when the main feature was not up to standard. I believe they are almost there. If there's a CFW 2.0 Val will probably address all the signal quality issues with bluetooth. Until then i'm sticking with wired m100.

Minor concerns of mine were the battery life over time (year two and up), sweat/rain damaging the electronics, and falls. The physical build quality is as durable as the m100 but the electronics add more variables that could fail in the event of a minor fall/spill. I know people use bluetooth on the go,so if you're on a train and they fall or it starts to rain, would the destruction be covered under warranty? Too scary for me to take that change.

so why 4 stars? They're excellent headphones wired, if you find the balance in volumes they're very good in wireless mode. I can be objective enough to know that something is good even though its not good for me in particular.

review_text:
Amazing sound, durable, some minor quirks. First and foremost, these headphones sound awesome. I upgraded from the M-80s and couldn't be happier. There's a good amount of bass but it's not overpowering and the mids and highs are crisp and clear. The noise isolation is also great. I use these in my morning commute on buses and walking, so that was important. Minimal street noise bleeds in but I prefer that so I don't get hit by a car. They also seem to be just as durable as the M-80s which have lasted me over 2 years without issues.
Initially I bought the new Bose Over Ear Bluetooth headphones but I thought the sound was thin, the headband was uncomfortable, and I found that my volume was up to 75-80% while outdoors, so they went back. I'm so happy I did because the Crossfade Wireless sound is more vibrant, louder (only 35-50% volume on the street), and the headband distributes the weight better.
Now some of the quirks: When you turn on the headphones the volume always goes to a predetermined level, you have to hit a volume button to get it back to where you left it. When turning the bluetooth on these weren't as quick to reconnect to my phone as the Bose were and maybe 1 in 10 times I have to go to the settings app and manually connect.

review_text:
Not one Bad Thing to Say. I wouldn't consider myself an audiophile but a music lover. I've listened to music my entire life and enjoy all genres with the exception of most country. With that said, I've always been passionate about mid-top tier audio products and have been searching for a great sounding set of bluetooth headphones. I scoured the web and the V-Moda's came up in a couple of "best of 2015" articles.

Frankly, what initially caught my eye was their incredible and one of a kind styling. I was looking for something that sounded great but I also didn't want to be another person wearing beats out of the house. Not that I think beats are horrible, because I've owned two sets of the bluetooth sports headphones. One had some quality issues. To the point, I wanted something different and something that isn't on every walmart/target shelf.

So after reading reviews and checking out their website, I pulled the trigger. Incidentally, If you look at the reviews on Amazon only 2% are 1 star. That says something. Most of the solid quality products that I have purchased over the years at least have a 5% 1 star rating.

To be fair, I ordered them from the V-Moda website because they offer free customized ear covers. I couldn't be happier. They updated my order regularly. I ordered them on Friday and received them on Monday. The packaging is sublime and the build of the headphones is quality. They remind me of a modern and streamlined version of my father's headphones from 40 years ago. The arms click into place with a satisfying feedback and you can feel and hear the quality of the spring mechanism. Everything about them says "quality". They are comfortable and light.

I've seen some reviews that say they are a bit on the heavy side and I disagree completely. They are much lighter than my gaming headset and I've been wearing them almost all day with no ill effects or hotspots.

The sound quality is phenomenal. I've listened to music that I've heard for over 20 years and I've picked up some subtle and sometimes not so subtle nuances that I've never heard before. It's like listening to my music for the first time.

The mid range is clear, the bass full, and the treble is crisp. I can almost see the vibrating guitar string with each "pluck". It's really amazing.

My wife, who doesn't really give a rip about sound quality one way or the other, even noticed how great they were when I played her "Into the Mystic". She liked them so much I will be ordering her a customized and monogramed pair of her own soon.

They aren't noise cancelling but they do a good job of blocking out the world around us.

The carrying case is well thought out and high quality. I have absolutely nothing bad to say about this product.

The built in microphone works great. I took two calls on them today and no one mentioned anything. I didn't have to yell and they sounded clear as day.

At $300, I don't think you can go wrong with these. There are others out there in this price range, but I honestly don't think you will get better sound quality regardless of what you spend. From a design and form factor I don't think these can be beat either.

If you are remotely close to "being on the fence" about buying these, I would encourage you to pull the trigger. Obviously with Amazon's stellar return policy if there is a problem they can be quickly returned. V-Moda also offers a 60 day return policy too. Check them out, give them a listen if you can, but these are my new favorite thing.

review_text:
Not one Bad Thing to Say. I wouldn't consider myself an audiophile but a music lover. I've listened to music my entire life and enjoy all genres with the exception of most country. With that said, I've always been passionate about mid-top tier audio products and have been searching for a great sounding set of bluetooth headphones. I scoured the web and the V-Moda's came up in a couple of "best of 2015" articles.

Frankly, what initially caught my eye was their incredible and one of a kind styling. I was looking for something that sounded great but I also didn't want to be another person wearing beats out of the house. Not that I think beats are horrible, because I've owned two sets of the bluetooth sports headphones. One had some quality issues. To the point, I wanted something different and something that isn't on every walmart/target shelf.

So after reading reviews and checking out their website, I pulled the trigger. Incidentally, If you look at the reviews on Amazon only 2% are 1 star. That says something. Most of the solid quality products that I have purchased over the years at least have a 5% 1 star rating.

To be fair, I ordered them from the V-Moda website because they offer free customized ear covers. I couldn't be happier. They updated my order regularly. I ordered them on Friday and received them on Monday. The packaging is sublime and the build of the headphones is quality. They remind me of a modern and streamlined version of my father's headphones from 40 years ago. The arms click into place with a satisfying feedback and you can feel and hear the quality of the spring mechanism. Everything about them says "quality". They are comfortable and light.

I've seen some reviews that say they are a bit on the heavy side and I disagree completely. They are much lighter than my gaming headset and I've been wearing them almost all day with no ill effects or hotspots.

The sound quality is phenomenal. I've listened to music that I've heard for over 20 years and I've picked up some subtle and sometimes not so subtle nuances that I've never heard before. It's like listening to my music for the first time.

The mid range is clear, the bass full, and the treble is crisp. I can almost see the vibrating guitar string with each "pluck". It's really amazing.

My wife, who doesn't really give a rip about sound quality one way or the other, even noticed how great they were when I played her "Into the Mystic". She liked them so much I will be ordering her a customized and monogramed pair of her own soon.

They aren't noise cancelling but they do a good job of blocking out the world around us.

The carrying case is well thought out and high quality. I have absolutely nothing bad to say about this product.

The built in microphone works great. I took two calls on them today and no one mentioned anything. I didn't have to yell and they sounded clear as day.

At $300, I don't think you can go wrong with these. There are others out there in this price range, but I honestly don't think you will get better sound quality regardless of what you spend. From a design and form factor I don't think these can be beat either.

If you are remotely close to "being on the fence" about buying these, I would encourage you to pull the trigger. Obviously with Amazon's stellar return policy if there is a problem they can be quickly returned. V-Moda also offers a 60 day return policy too. Check them out, give them a listen if you can, but these are my new favorite thing.

review_text:
Great sound, function and build but horribly undersized and padded ear cushions. Tried out a set for about a month. They look great, are well built, the BT functions extremely well- the best I've encountered and they sound absolutely fantastic. So I just sent them back. The reason, they were very uncomfortable with the standard ear cushions. I thought I would get used to them but not so. I made them a little looser but there was still way too much pressure on my ears.

I tried the XL ear cushions. It helped a little but in reality they were not much better. And the XL cushions for some reason each had 6 small holes around the inside of the pleather essentially turning the cushions into sponges. No good when my main use for these is during exercise.

Overall these are $299 headphones with $1 ear cushions. The most uncomfortable over ear or on ear headphones I've tried. I'm sure they sound better and are built better than the Bose BT headphones, but damn, the Bose are so much more comfortable. The standard ear cushions are sooooo much better than either cushion available for the Crossfades.

Too bad, because they sound incredible.

review_text:
One of the best pair of headphones iv'e heard to date. Take note that these are my first pair headphones that goes over $150 , so lets get started .

(BUILD QUALITY)
These headphones by far are the most durable pair of headphones iv'e ever owned and held, taken that they're $300 i wouldn't expect less ,just by holding them makes me feel like they can survive a three story drop to the ground and i bet they can . Everything from the headband down just screams quality in such a way that your money is being worth of and that applies to the sound as well, but we'll get into that in a bit.

(COMFORT)
All i can say is that these headphones are quite comfortable not the most comfortable iv'e tried but still to the average consumer they well very much find them satisfying to wear. No wearing fatigue at all overtime even though the clamping force is kinda strong, it makes me feel like they're telling me "i got you ", like they're never gonna let go and i like that in a way and it's all because of the headband , because of it's compact shape to give it a low profile it kinda conforms to your head and it really adds to the comfort ,but they will start to fall if you're head knocking like a possessed person to some heavy dubstep i can tell ya that . On to the ear pads , even though the ear pads are not too plush they're really comfortable ,but the comfort varies on the size of your ears , my experience with them is that my ears fit perfectly not too big or not too small and it has been great experience for me , my ears don't even touch the divers but that's just me , if you know that you're ears are big i suggest getting the XL pads i am myself are planning on purchasing them because who doesn't want 2X the comfort .

(BLUETOOTH CONNECTIVITY & BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY)
Not much to say here but when it comes to Bluetooth it's no joke, i can hardly tell the difference between when it's connected via Bluetooth or wired, yes it's that good and also they can go really far without braking up ,i can literally walk around some parts of my house with them on while my phone is in my room and nothing , i can say the max range can be up to about 50 feet or so . The buttons on these headphones i can say is that the placement is adequate and the feel of when you press on them are not really rouged but is enough to satisfy anyone. When it come to the functionality of the buttons it's really easy to operate [middle button : one tap = play/pause , two taps = skip track , three taps = previous track] and there's just the volume up and volume down, when using these buttons i find them very responsive but not too responsive where it's instant but over over all they're really good .

(SOUND QUALITY)
Now taken that these are my first headphones over $150 you'd expect me to say that these are the best iv'e heard and you're right ,the fidelity in this masterpiece of an headphone are insane , The highs are very present ,the mids are in a position where i can say that they are slightly less present but still has a strong influence and now the lows , i can say that they are as present as the mids but yet it doesn't distort the mids at all ,it actually blends with it really well also it's so strong that the headphone literally shake ,kinda like the sony pulse. Now on to the volume levels , i can tell ya that these headphones get way louder than the average headphone wired or non wired , when it's on Bluetooth mode the volume levels to me are way louder than wired ,that's because of the mini vamp inside the headphones to push that extra volume that normal Bluetooth headphones don't provide.

Ratings
BUILD QUALITY : 10/10
COMFORT : 7.5/10
BLUETOOTH : 10/10
BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY : 9/10
SOUND QUALITY: 10?10

OVERALL : 9.5/10

review_text: Creation from the Italian Gods. Oh the beautiful and fabulously amazing V-MODA Crossfade wireless headphones! They are a creation from the Italian gods themselves. These headphones are by far my favorites of the plethora that I own, which is many. Their clarity is astounding, both in wired mode as well as in wireless mode. This feet is nothing short of a miracle from the man Val Kolton. He being a previous purest with the analog modes, vowed to never make a wireless headphone unless it matched the analog mode. These headphones are extremely stable and durable. I use them mostly at the gym, but also use them at work for talking on the phone (I'm in the QA department). Others say they hear me great, even when I am wireless. I get the 30 ft. distance for bluetooth range, plus more.. through a cinder block building at that! These bad boys can take a serious beating, and if they break, there is always the immortal plan through V-MODA. You can hammer on these guys all day without them even breaking a sweat. The audio is bar none! Even at high levels, the clarity stands supreme. Having a 50mm dual diaphram driver, these cans can hit it all. To my ears, they have a pretty distinctive V-sound signature. They have slightly recessed mids, and pronounced highs/lows. They sure can go low, but not that digital low crap like Beats by Dre. The 50mm driver makes them never run out of breathe, even for those incredibly low hits you get from EDM. They also connect to my apple watch amazingly well. The bluetooth receiver has been modified to account for the small antennas in smart watches. Val himself ran over 1000 km with his watch. What a way to remove yourself from the world a little bit. If you are looking at these headphones, it means you have done some research and have a good head on your shoulders. You're already this far, just do yourself the favor and buy them.. YOU WON'T REGRET IT!!!! You will fall in love at first hearing. The XL cushions increase the sound stage and make long listening even more comfortable. They are a must! And at $20, you're only doing yourself justice. Don't believe me? Try it yourself and prove me wrong! V-MODA has a 60 day test drive program. I dare you to prove me wrong!

review_text:
Unbelievable experience. Unbelievable over-ear wireless headphones. These V-Moda Crossfade Wireless headphones are very visually appealing. They arrived very fast and were brand spanking new. I bought the Sennheiser Momentum 2.0 Over-Ear wireless headphones and returned them right away after I got my V-Moda Wireless headphones. I did this for a number of reasons: the sennheisers are fairly expensive cans ($500+!), the sennheisers are also bigger and I believe they look slightly more distasteful when they are over your head. By no means does it look bad however, I prefer the sleeker design of the V-modas. I also love the customizability of the V-modas. I was slightly disappointed hearing that the V-Moda wireless model will not be having the folding/clicking mechanism that the M-100's had but the V-moda wireless already leaves such a small footprint that it doesn't suffer much from the lack of this folding mechanism. Now lets get into the sound:

The V-Moda Crossfade wireless offers superb sound - especially at its price point. The highlight of it being its very noticeable bass (by no means jaw-rattling, but indeed felt when compared to the Sennheiser momentum line up). Although the bass is much more pronounced and heart-felt the V-moda team did a remarkable job in fine-tuning the bass so that it doesn't leak into the mids and highs and disturb those ends of the musical spectrum. In other words, the highs and mids are still present and do not suffer from the blossoming bass (great job V-Moda!). The ear cups encompassed my ears perfectly and were very comfortable. If they happen to not work for you, you can buy the XL versions which are sold separately (around 20 bucks). Another amazing aspect of these headphones is the build quality. These feel substantial when you hold onto them without being heavy. These metals are built with some plastic and a lot of metal which really improves its structural integrity. In other words they are very strong cans which will last you a good amount of time. The clamping pressure of these headphones is perfect (on the snug side but by no means uncomfortable). I use them while I workout and so far they are amazing. However they are probably not the best option if you run a lot. Bluetooth connectivity is amazing. I tested them out and the range is around 30ft. These are wired too so you get the best of both worlds. Personally I listen to a lot of rap, rock and hip hop genres of music and I believe these headphones are tailored towards that spectrum of electronic/modern music. If you listen to classical I think there are better headphone options out there like the Sennheiser momentum line up. These V-Moda's will do a good job with classical music but I believe it's tailored towards more modern and younger crowd of individuals.

IN CONCLUSION: These headphones are by far my favorite headphones to date. They are exceptional in the sound, portability, visual appeal and comfortability aspects and for $300 you are getting much more than you paid for. If anything, I wish they update this version and add the folding mechanism which will manage to make this headphone EVEN better. I hope you pick one of these up because they will most definitely not disappoint.

review_text:
Best earphones I've ever owned. Best earphones I've ever owned. Period. Sound is incredibly clear and smooth. Battery last quite long. Look great and are on the light side. Wore these on a 6 hour plane ride and didn't really have any discomfort.

Sound comes through incredibly crisp, with the right treble and strong and more importantly, deep enough bass but without being overbearing.

The sound with BT enabled is also amazing! Lots of previous products suffer from the sound with BT enabled being off or not clear, but you can hardly discern the difference between being plugged in or BT.

The finish on the headphones is impeccable as well. I did decide to purchase the XL ear fittings. They are more comfortable than the factory ones and hugely help with canceling out sound from them.

That said, I firmly believe these are the best wireless headphones on the market. V-Moda has been making great products for some time now and this is no exception. I'm a big audiophile and can't stand bad sound and I see these being in my daily routine for some time now. Well worth the price tag.

Best earphones I've ever owned. Best earphones I've ever owned. Period. Sound is incredibly clear and smooth. Battery last quite long. Look great and are on the light side. Wore these on a 6 hour plane ride and didn't really have any discomfort.

review_text: I was particularly impressed with the attractive packaging and sturdy storage case. Let me preface by saying I have been a Bose user for many years. Recently my QC15 headphones failed. My first thought was to call Bose and order a replacement set, however I decided to do some research and see what alternatives were available. After reading all the positive reviews, I decided to order a set of wireless Crossfades. When they arrived, I was particularly impressed with the attractive packaging and sturdy storage case. After unpacking, I immediately connected them to my I-Phone via bluetooth (very easy process) and began listening to one of my favorite play lists. I noticed the the ear cups didn't fit very well, especially for headphones that were advertised as around the ear. In my case they were more on ear, and began to be uncomfortable after about a half hour. After an hour, I had to take them off due to extreme discomfort. I tried them again on several more occasions with the same result. As for the sound reproduction, I liked it for the most part, however in some instances the bass was to heavy for my personal taste. It tended to overpower the vocals and lead instruments. I prefer the bass to be more smooth and mellow with vocals in the center of the soundstage. I am no audiophile by any means, I just know what I like. Folks with different audio preferences may find these headphones to be excellent, however I would suggest that anyone ordering them should probably consider the oversized ear cups. I really wanted to like these headphones, but the discomfort caused by the small ear cups unfortunately precluded me from keeping them. I did return them and ultimately ordered a set of Bose QC25s. They fit perfectly and sound great

review_text:
Stop looking for headphones and buy these. These are "the one.". I bought these headphones based on reviews I've seen scattered on the internet. On recommendation, I bought these - slightly scared I spent $300 on headphones that are subpar. Once I received the package itself, I knew I wasn't dealing with any middle-of-the-mall pair of headphones. The packaging was nice; you could immediately tell that the gods presented you with a musical gift based on packaging alone. The headphones came with x1 micro-USB cable & x1 analog audio cable. They sync'ed to my phone without any problem what-so-ever but I have not had the opportunity to sync these headphones with another device while simultaneously playing music. These are over-the-ear headphones and they ISOLATE noise; they do not cancel noise. However when you're jamming out to your favorite tracks..you can't hear anything at all.

The sound quality is the main selling point here. Sound quality is superb and will surpass just about any pair of headphones that seemed worthy enough to cling to your ears. The high & lows are incredibly powerful. I was able to pickup partitions of my favorite music that I've never heard before; the clarity the VMODA Crossfade provide is unmatched. This, in no way, distorted mids. The Crossfade wireless perfectly ties highs mids & lows together like the Holy Trinity. Unlike some headphones I've experienced, you can FEEL the bass resonating from them. This makes the music you're listening much more enjoyable.

A concern many have had would be the quality of music with Bluetooth compared to a wired connection. Fear not! These bad boys sound almost exactly alike when compared to a wired connection. There is a very, very small difference between the two. You would be incredibly surprised how similar the 2 connections are. These are, without a doubt, the best sounding Bluetooth headphones you will listen to.

Overall durability? You're not breaking these headphones any time soon. The headband is made of steel yet provides a lot of flexibility. I purposely tried to bend the steel bands connected to the drivers and couldn't. You will have to put in serious effort in order to bend these beasts. There are kevlar wrapped wires hanging above each driver; they do not get in the way in any fashion. Some have complained about getting this wire caught when taking the headphones off but I do not see how this is possible. To protect your favorite headphones, you will also receive a nice case to store your headphones & accessories into; the case has a decent amount of durability behind it so you can store your jam boxes and be on your way. The battery life is also something to be remembered. These have latest almost 8 hours before needing to be charged again. Need a quick charge before heading to the gym? Thankfully these babies are equipped with quick charge. 15 minutes of charging will get you 2 hours of listening!

While these sleek pair of headphones scream superb quality - it does come with a few cons. One major con are the 'memory foam' ear pads. Since I use these headphones throughout a majority of my day..my ears would begin to hurt and I'd have to take my headphones off. My ears were pressing against the drivers which made them more & more uncomfortable to wear. I solved this problem by spending the extra money on a pair of XL ear pads. Installing these XL ear pads was incredibly easy. Some have said the earpads 'increase' sound quality but I don't find this to be true however they also did not take AWAY from my music experience. The ear pads are a comfort upgrade only.

Want to use these headphones for gaming on your Xbox One? These are excellent gaming headphones; Don't expect something similar to a 5.1/7.1 surround sound though - remember..these aren't designed for gaming but make an excellent alternative regardless. If you plan on chatting while gaming: do yourself a favor - buy the BoomPro microphone. The stock analog cable DOES transmit voice however you may sound incredibly muffled to a point where no one can hear you. You CANNOT sync these headphones via Bluetooth to an Xbox one. You will need to plug these headphones directly into the Xbox one controller.

Verdict? Buy. Buy. Buy. Take the $300 and spend it. Once you encapsalte yourself into the music with these beastly headphones you will become a V-MODA enthusiest. I sure am now and will recommend these to ANYBODY in search for new headphones. While the price is steep..you absolutely cannot deny the overall music quality & headphone durability.

TL;DR
PROs:
Highs & lows sound incredibly superb.
Bass so distinct it can be felt while simtaneously not distorting any highs, mids or lows.
Bluetooth vs Analog connection sound incredibly similar and the difference can go unnoticed.
Bluetooth mic sounds incredibly clear.
Durability seems top-notch; you won't be bending/breaking the steel band without serious effort.
Lots of battery life. Quick-charged enabled. (~15 minute charge = ~2 hours of music)

CONs:
Stock ear pads may be too small & your ears may touch the drivers. (Buy XL Ear pads, $20.)
Stock analog cable, if used for communication, will make you sound muffled & almost uncomprehendable. (If needed for gaming, buy a VMODA BoomPro mic)
You don't own these yet.

Stock analog cable makes voice sound muffled during communication.

review_text: Lemon or Unmarked Refurb?. Honestly, I wonder if I received a pair of unmarked refurbished headphones; they don't meet any of the expectations of this brand. Prior to ordering, I watched countless videos, read plenty of reviews, and even tested the M-100s against which the Crossfade Wireless' were referred to as more mature sounding (CNET's review). Most reviews said they were well-built premium headphones. Most said they sounded nearly identical in passive and Bluetooth mode. Most said they were fun to listen to. Wrong wrong wrong. First, while exceptionally comfortable, the fit/finish on the left ear cup allowed it to slide laterally within the swivel like the swivel was built to a larger tolerance or bent. Second, the upper midrange distorts on certain notes and there is too much bass when using the Bluetooth to power the speakers; when listening in passive mode with the included cable connection, they have a decent sound and a really good sound stage, but did not sound as crisp as the M100s I listened to at the Best Buy Magnolia display (the only V-Moda retailer near me). However, I didn't buy them for their corded capabilities, but rather for their wireless capability and they just don't work for me under that use case. Lastly, they're no more fun than my $25 Panasonic wired earbuds which reproduce higher bass than one would expect, but muddies the rest of the sound spectrum. For comparison, I have the Jaybird X2 earbuds and they blow these V-Moda's away.......with the X2s I hear things I missed like the piano and violin on System of a Down's Chop Suey, but they're recessed on the V-Moda's in wired mode and barely audible in wireless mode. BTW, I was really excited for these and returned a pair of JBL Everest Elite 700s (poor headband design which was cracked and a bad cable) in order to get the V-Moda Crossfade Wireless. Utterly disappointed and returning them. Given all the hype around this brand and these headphones, I honestly wonder if I got shipped a pair of refurbished/returned headphones instead of a pair fresh off the assembly line; if so, they weren't advertised or priced as such.

review_text:
Excellent pair of good-looking Wireless headphones with superb sound and above-average battery life. I am not a fan of reviews right after or during an unboxing, I do believe that in order to review most items objectively, you need some time to really use them every day.

I've had this pair for two months now so let's try to separate this review into some categories:
- Sound: Warm, heavy on the bass and, as other user and critics review said, it sounds equally great with or without the cable. You can use these for ALL kind of music and expect great detail and differentiation of frequencies
- Battery life: 13 solid hours
- Price: 299 as of Feb 2016, which is extremely competitive, particularly because V-Moda's previous model, the M-100 was introduced at that same price point. Compared with other brands, it is also pretty competitive but you have to consider that these do not have active noise cancellation
- Noise cancellation/Sound leaking: As previously said, these come with passive noise cancellation, meaning no ultrasonic sound blocking external sounds, but thanks to that, it adds to a better clarity and no head aches. In terms of sound leakage, these isolate your music pretty well, you will be able to use them on commute trips without disturbing people around you
- Comfort: Great but not superb, I suggest you get the XL cushions to make this category Excellent. The head band is not too tight, you can wear these for 3 hours or more with the XL cushions. Out of the box, the original ear pads are a little small so you will be able to continually use these only for some time before your ears get extremely hot or start hurting
- Design: The design carries from the M-100, while timeless, at this point this category is probably the lowest point of this product. Do not get me wrong, the headphones have a beautiful design and with a terrific construction and the ability to replace the side shields is a really clever idea that got enhanced with the support for 3D ones, V-Moda has used the same look for a few good years now. Imagine if the most beautiful cars stayed with the same look over many, many years
- Support: One of the best things about this company is its commitment to an outstanding customer service, so this category needs to be mentioned. For example, they have a 30-day satisfaction guaranteed when purchasing these (not sure if that is applicable to Amazon's purchases), second example: they allow you to keep up with new products for a significant discount thanks to the Immortal Life Program, if you have not heard about it, it is basically a trade-in program which is much, much better to use than selling your old headphones via Craigslist to get the latest product
- Cons: The only downsize of these is that for some odd reason the minimum volume is a bit high

If you are considering a good pair, look no further, get these, make sure to get the XL ear pads and start customizing them with new shields, 3D printed or not

review_text:
So far, SOLID wireless headphones from V-Moda. This won't be a full review yet because I just got my pair a couple of days ago from V-Moda, but so far they are awesome.

Coming from using the M100 religiously, they sound equal to actually significantly better in some areas.

The M100 is great for bass while keeping everything else crystal clear. The Crossfade Wireless seems to improve on the mid clarity while tightening up the bass and keepin it punchy.
This goes for wired and wireless and I honestly can barely tell a difference in sound quality between wired and wireless.

The construction is very much like the M100 and I used my XL ear pads on the wireless. I opted for the gunmetal version and although mines has a blue tint to them I still really like them, they just seem different that I expected.

The pairing was easy enough and I know for my iPhone 6, that the notifications screen shows the battery percentage while the main screen shows a new battery bar by the phones battery bar that shows how much juice the Crossfade Wireless has left in it. I have used them wirelessly for around 5 hours so far and it shows about 60% battery left.

The controls feel good and seem sturdy and reliable. They work a lot like the three button remotes on apple headphones.

I really like that there is a wired mode that immediately shuts down wireless mode as soon as you plug it into a 3.5mm jack. This turns off the battery and allows for unlimited listening in wired mode whereas some wireless headphones always need the battery to be used.

My only issue comes from the M100. Cliqfold and the lack of it. The M100 came with an awesome feature called cliqfold that allowed the headphones to fold up really nice and compact. That feature seems to have been omitted here and I don't see a logical reason why just yet. They are still very portable so I didn't feel it enough to dock a star for.

Overall they are great wireless headphones from a company that initially never seemed like they would make wireless headphones. I feel a lot of time went into tuning and although my experience with wireless Bluetooth headphones is limited, I know these are the best I've heard. These are easy to recommend and I'll keep updating my review as I have more time with them.

UPDATE 1:
Forgot to mention that comfort for the Crossfade Wireless is similar to the M100. With the stock earcups comfort is good but after a few hours it is not great. I recommend the XL Earcups if you experience a good deal of discomfort after long term use. I do have a big head so try out the standard cups first but for me the XL earcups add a lot more comfort.

A Fantastic Wireless Headphone.. Got my Crossfade Wireless today in gunmetal. I threw on my steel 3D printed V-MODA plates, the XL Pads and I'm a happy camper (not a big fan of the shiny gunmetal stock shields). These headphones are incredible. One thing to note, the steel shields are also a bit on the heavy side compared to the stock aluminum but they look fantastic IMO so the tradeoff is worth it. This is a fantastic addition to the Crossfade lineup. Oh how I wish they had Click Fold hinges though like the M100. Maybe in the next version.

Either way, kudos to V-MODA for another great headphone.

Surprisingly good! In fact, they are GREAT!. Wow. Wow. Wow. These headphones are awesome. I have a pair of the Crossfade LPs and LOVE them. I was very hesitant to try the bluetooth ones just because of my experience with bluetooth speakers, etc. I have Bose SoundLink (the original) and it works pretty well. However, it does cut out once in a while, and the sound quality is fantastic or anything. I also have a Logitech bluetooth receiver that I use to wirelessly connect to my Klipsch system. It does ok, but cuts out quite often. So I was not sure I would love these. But I have been pleasantly surprised on all fronts.

These headphones have rock-solid bluetooth streaming. I have about 100 hours on mine, and they have never cut out or dropped a single time. review_text:
Superb headphones!. So why am I giving headphones that I consider to be fantastic only 3 stars? Because I also happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat pros. Those headphones are superior in almost every way for the same price or far less if you get the older version.

I will focus first on these headphones and then the comparison to the Plantronics. The Crossfades scream quality and beauty when unboxing. The materials are the highest quality and they just feel good. The metal construction is top notch and the plastics are solid and substantial. The metal accent shields are beautiful and just make the headphones look good.

Controls are sparse, but effective. There is a power/pairing button on the bottom of the right headphone that functions well and is fairly intuitive. At the top are a series of three button. The center one pauses/starts the music and answers calls. The two surrounding it control volume and skip music forward or backward.

These headphones are very comfortable. I have a large head and they accommodate me with ease and I don't have too much discomfort even after a couple of hours use. They are even more comfortable after adding the XL pads. The pads make the ear opening larger and put more distance between the ear and the speaker. The XL pads are so much better that I think VMODA should have made them standard instead of selling them as an extra. Especially at this price point.

Sound. If I hadn't heard a better set, I would have been completely happy with this headphone. Bass is good and highs are where they should be. Mids are a bit too recessed for my taste so some vocals are lost. They play well at low volumes and can get plenty loud. Sound bleed is minimal and the outside world does not intrude too much. In the end, these really are great sounding headphones. Again, the XL pads improve the sound greatly. They provide a greater depth of sound and a much warmer tone.

This brings me to the reason that I am returning these and why they are only receiving 3 stars from me, despite how much I like them. I happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat Pro and they are superior to the Crossfades in nearly every way. The controls are more intuitive and easier to use. The Plantronics have APTx, active noise cancelling, voice prompts, and longer battery life. Most importantly, they simply sound better. As good as the Crossfades are, the Backbeats are better. Deeper bass, better mids, and they sound far clearer than the Crossfades. The Crossfades are very muddy by comparison. The Vmodas are constructed of better quality materials, are lighter, and look better, but that is not enough to justify buying them when a better alternative exists. Especially since you can get the old version of the Plantronics for far less.

To sum up. Great headphones that you will likely be really happy with, but there are better available for similar or less money. I also think that it is a sin that VMODA charges extra for the XL pads which are a necessity to get the best out of them. I really wanted to keep these and be happily ever after, but I simply can't. Back they go.

review_text:
Best headphones for the price. I'm a bit of an audiophile and have a decent collection of headphones. I got these off of V-Moda's website (I had a coupon) and I have been blown away. The sound is incredibly crisp. The range in the highs is very good. However, bass is where these shine. I didn't think unamped headphones at this price point could deliver such a full spectrum of lows and provide as much a kick as these do.

Comparisons:
Beats Studio - In my opinion there's no contest, the V-Moda's take it. The Beats have a bass that over powers the highs and have a smaller spectrum than the V-Modas. The V-Modas have more detail across all spectrums. They also have phenomenal build quality and a much more impressive and portable case than the Beats.

Sennheiser Momentums - these were my previous go-to's. The Sennheisers are definitely better general purpose headphones. They have cleaner highs (which is saying something), but have noticeably weaker bass. The V-Moda's are better for all music except genres like jazz and classical. Also, I prefer the styling and build of the V-Modas. I should note two things: the V-Moda's are incredibly more comfortable than the Sennheisers and the V-Moda's are over ear, not on ear, which the Sennheisers are. My head begins to hurt after a couple of hours of wearing the Sennheisers because they are so tight and I have a slightly larger head.

Sony MDX wireless - I think the V-Moda's are superior in every category. The Sonys are lighter and have pivoting ear pieces, but that's it.

Audio Techinica - (I don't have these any more and can't remember the model, but they come in around the 100 price point). Again, not a contest. The Audio Technicas feel and sound cheap by comparison.

Reservations:
The price can be off putting for some and I couldn't disagree more. These are an incredible value and V-Moda's warranty is quite good.

The bass may over power the highs. For most listening, this won't make a difference, but if I'm going to listen to jazz, spoken word, a TV show, I'm going to grab my Sennheisers.

review_text:
Comfortable, high-quality headphones with excellent sound quality. [[VIDEOID:93f3f8e59bcd3a44f877c1bd5e927a25]]Pros:
-Product presentation
-Super comfortable
-Incoming calls and other functions are announced in spoken word
-Noise cancellation is excellent (what lawnmower???)
-Variety of earbud sizes
-Sturdy, compact carrying case
-Same Micro-USB charger as Android phones
-“Bolo tie” style cord manager included

Cons:
-I honestly haven’t found any yet!

I was very pleasantly surprised by these little ear buds. I know Amazon frowns on talking about “packaging” in reviews, but I do like to point out good product presentation when I see it! Unboxing these headphones really feels like you’re digging into a quality product. They did an excellent job there.

The quality doesn’t stop with the unboxing, either. Everything about these seems solid and quality-oriented, from the feel of the materials to the fit of smaller moving components like the charging port cover and the power / pairing button.

I put these to first test of doing all of my yard work this morning and they absolutely exceeded my expectations. The sound quality is unmistakably excellent and the noise cancellation is on-point. Normally when I wear headphones while doing yardwork I have to have the volume on my Galaxy S5 MAXED OUT to be able to hear anything over the lawnmower. With these I was able to listen to podcasts at right around half volume and still hear each and every word clearly. Very impressive.

Another feature I like is the voice which announces different functions and incoming calls identified by numbers. No trying to decipher cryptic beep codes as with some cheaper headsets.

The included accessories are all welcomed additions and of equally respectable quality including the charging cable, different sized earbuds, and carrying case. It is worth noting that the charging cable is pretty short (only a few inches), but this allows for increased portability and it folds nicely up into the netted pocket in the carrying case. The charging port is a standard Micro-USB (same as android phones), so you should have plenty of available longer charger cables if you need them (especially if you’re an Android user).

I really couldn’t find anything I don’t like about these headphones and they’ll be my go-to pair for certain. Please be safe when using earbuds while walking, running, or cycling on public roads and sidewalks – they make it much more difficult to hear what’s going on around you.

I provided an honest and unbiased review of this product which was sold to me at a discount. I strive to stand by the "honest and unbiased" goal. I will always point out what I deem to be negative aspects of the product, and ding stars accordingly. I'm just a regular dude that likes to write and bump NPR while I mow the lawn.

review_text:
Never Write Reviews. Never Write Reviews.

These headphones are nice! Depending on the music that you listen too your experience may be better than other. As for me I listen to a fair amount of rap with a heavy beat. I wouldn't consider myself an audiophile but I do have experience with Bose, Etomotic and Klipsch. This being my first pair of "in ear" Bluetooth headphones (own Outdoor Research Chips).

One of the biggest things I look for when I purchase new headphones is comfort. These are great in that aspect, they are lightweight and more or less "rest" in your ears while staying secure.

Are they noise isolating? Kinda, but not really, they do block out some ambient noise but not like my Etomotic HF5's or the Klipsch earbuds I owned years ago. The battery life on these is congruent with that in the description.

Some very minor problems I have with the headphones.
With Bluetooth your sound quality isn't(yet) up to par with a wired connection. Not these headphones fault, but they are bass heavy regardless. Some people enjoy their bass a lot but I prefer even tones. I did set the EQ on my iPhone to bass reducer and found that to make them in my opinion, better.

The charging/Bluetooth light doesn't have the ability to turn off when on. So it blinks every few seconds. Like I said minor problem.

Other than those two things I absolutely love these headphones. I go to the gym daily and these are now my go to. I don't have to deal with cords which makes life easier at the gym for sure. review_text:
Worth the wait but don't expect miraculous sound. A big thing to consider about whether or not to get these ear buds is the shipping. This set is imported from China and with free shipping it took a couple of weeks to get to TX. If you're willing to wait for it you'll be getting a very good sounding set of sub $20 earbuds.
The build quality of these buds does not feel overly cheap nor premium but above average.
Interestingly there's a small metal bead a few inches below each earbud which are supposed to be weights that pull the cable down to straighten it when wearing.
The cables have a strange gummy quality that sort of work out as it sort of feels like silicone. The cables are not stiff but springy in a way that there is less sound when the cord is touched while wearing them.
The storage box these earbuds came in did not impress me much. It was kind of cheap and awkwardly designed.
I really appreciate the memory foam ear tips as they make a better and more comfortable feel than the silicone ones. I have enough space in my ears to wear these comfortably and the memory foam helped out the noise cancellation very much, it's actually doing a good job blocking out noise for me at least.
The body of the earbuds are very unusual. I was wearing them wrong the first couple of times and they are difficult to tell when they are in properly. You have to look for the "L" and "R" markers on each earbud and kind of fit them in your outer ear.
For the sound. I'll have to disclose that I am not an audiophile so I'll describe it as well as I can.
The sound is easily the best part of these earbuds and the reason to get them.
The bass is strong and full compared to my other sub $20 earbuds. The sound is a bit more dynamic and more pleasing than my other set that has good bass so you get the bass with less muffled sounding vocals.
These bud's have a limit though. A decent pair of large over the ear headphones sound a lot better of course but these earbuds are probably one of the best you can get at this price range.
In my opinion these earbuds are worth the wait but at its price range don't expect miraculous sound.

I bought these earphones at a discount for review purposes thanks for reading.

review_text:
Excellent excellent build and sound quality for the cost. I'm by no means an audiophile but I have tried a bunch of low to mid range headphones and use a pair of Shure 215's as my daily drivers.
These headphones are amazing for the cost. Plain and simple.
Sound profile: The highs can be a bit tinny, a little TOO warm. The mids aren't the most robust and the bass is too much and kind of muddy.
All that being said, I'm comparing them to $100 IEMs so. the fact I can even make that comparison with a $15 is fantastic.
If using with some kind of software EQ I'm sure you could tweak these to be excellent.

As for the physical quality of them they're very nice. The cable doesn't transfer sound when brushing against your clothes and such. It has small weights on each cable to allow you to hang them behind your ears which helps with them not falling out and lets you run with them and such. The cable itself isn't very long and the With Mic version doesn't have that lil' slidey part to bring the two cables together more.

I will say the cable is a bit short when compared to other IEMs I've used.
Also the Mic button is very flaky on my Nexus 6P. It seems to change what functionality it has based on the foreground app and is kind of inconsistent. I've pressed it and it's: Paused the music. Gone back 10 seconds on a podcast. Launched Google Now. Etc.
Haven't tested functionality of the Mic itself. Giving these to a friend and just burning them in/testing out.

I mean really any negatives I can say would just be nit picking and frankly for $15 the overall quality of the sound and build quality for that cost hugely outweigh any downsides.

As I'd mentioned these are a gift and I'm glad they turned out to be pretty damn good lil IEMs for the cost so much so down the road I'll probably snag a second pair (though without the mic) for a backup to keep at the office if I ever forget my Shures at home.

Sound quality - They are far superior to anything you would purchase at most retailers. The KZ ATE is an exceptional value. There are several key points that I considered during this purchase as I wear them several hours a day.
1. Sound quality - They are far superior to anything you would purchase at most retailers. An order of magnitude better than the stock apple units for example. Just no comparison, on a par with other units that are in the $100 range. Really nice highs and midrange. Excellent bass, but not overwhelming thump. I listen to a range of music, jazz, classic rock and opera. Great for all. If you like huge thumping bass, they have another model that is tuned for even more bass. I have not felt that these lack in bass in any way. I really appreciate the fact that they do not get muddy at the very low end. Listening to Tender Years by John Cafferty (Eddie & the Cruisers movies) right now and well..WOW.

2. Comfort - I wear these several hours a day and they are light and comfortable. The ear piece has a gel tip that blocks out ambient noise, which contributes to the overall listening experience and is very easy on the ear. No pain points after hours of use.

3. Build quality - I don't know how they can build these units at this price. Heavier cord, beefy fasteners and connection points. Nice.

4. Microphone quality - People on the other end of the phone have commented on the quality of my transmission.

These are so inexpensive, absolutely no risk.
