review_text:
Truly Amazing For The Price. This is my personal review of the KZ-ATE In-Ear Monitors [IEM]. These words reflect my opinion and my opinion ONLY. No need to get upset! :)

SUMMARY
I bought the KZ-ATE Headphones as sort of an experiment, and was BLOWN away by their quality! For the price, you really can't go wrong with this pair of IEMs. If you want to know what all the hype is about concerning this headphone, just buy it! What's the most you could lose out on?

DEVICE SPECIFICATIONS
Device Type: In-Ear Headphone
Driver Type: Dynamic, Copper Driver
Driver Diameter: 8.2mm
Frequency Response: 15 Hz - 29,000 Hz
Sensitivity: 106 dB
Impedance: 16 ohms
Retail Price: Unknown
Current Price (Amazon): Approx. $12
Manufacturer: Knowledge-Zenith (China-based)

PERSONAL SCORES
Build Quality: 8.0
Sound Isolation: 8.0
Comfort Rating: 8.0
Sound Rating (Highs): 7.0
Sound Rating (Mids) : 7.8
Sound Rating (Lows) : 8.0
Sound Rating (Overall): 8.0

TEST ENVIRONMENT
DAC/AMP: AudioQuest Dragonfly 1.2
Operating System: Windows 7 Professional 64-bit
Source Material: Tidal (Master Quality Setting)

BACKGROUND / HISTORY
My journey into the audio appreciation world began a few years ago and has led me to obtain some nice hi-fi quality gear such as the Highly Acclaimed Sennheiser HD600 open-back headphones, as well as the Hifiman HE-400i, Massdrop AKG K7XX, and most notably my prized Beyerdynamic DT-1770 closed-back headphones. These, paired with the excellent Schiit Jotunheim have given me a modest perspective into the amazing world of high-fidelity audio. Although I am a relative newcomer in this arena, I feel proficient enough to provide a fair and honest review.

PROS / BENEFITS
Low Frequency Response: First off, let's get one thing out of the way: The KZ-ATE IEMs have BASS FOR DAYS!!! Woa!! I was not expecting this when I first put them on. When I first saw them on Amazon, I thought "oh how cute". Let me be CLEAR when I say that I bought them solely on price and aethetics, and because I wanted a cheap pair of IEMs and thought "what's the worst I can lose out on?" Well, it's a good thing that I did because I'm not joking when I say that these IEMs have EARTH-SHATTERING bass and so I now have a entry-level unit that I can recommend to my "bass heads" friends, lol.

Sound Isolation: The KZ-ATE IEMs have very good sound isolation. I found that even at low volumes, the KZ-ATE IEMs were able to drown out most of the noise in my office where I work. Now, keep in mind that I work in a very quiet office setting (about 32-37 dB). Still, the KZ-ATE IEMs produced a good seal inside of my ear with one of the included ear tips.

Detail / Resolution: At a current price tag of $12-15 on Amazon, the KZ-ATE IEMs aren't the cleanest or most detailed IEMs around, but FOR THE PRICE boy do you get a bang for your buck! You would think that such a cheap IEM with such powerful bass response would be SEVERELY lacking in the mid-to-high audio spectrum, but in my case I was surprised by the relative clarity that these IEMs are able to achieve. For example, listening to Lindsey Stirling's "Crystallize" on Tidal with Master Quality Settings is quite a joy. Again, these by far are NOT the most balanced IEMs out there, but for the price you will be amazed at how they sound.

Portability: IEMs by default are designed to be portable, and that is also the case with the KZ-ATE IEMs. With a low impedance of 16 ohms and a Sensitivity Rating of 106 dB, you won't need to pair them up with an external amplifier, but of course you will always benefit from having one.

CONS / DOWNSIDES
There are some downsides that we should discuss.

Audio Quality: First off, there has to be a trade-off when producing cheap products. There is a reason why high-end audio gear costs so much, but that gap significantly gotten smaller in recent years. These IEMs are proof of that!! Still, I don't want to mislead you. What you will NOT get from these IEMs is high-fidelity audio. This is most noticeable in their lack of clarity and separation. While you do get detail and bass response that you would not expect at this price range, you will NOT be blown away by pristine highs and mids. Instead, what you will get is a very fun and enjoyable listening experience if you can learn to live with the IEM's shortcomings in the middle-to-high ranges.

Comfort Factor: Overall, I found the KZ-ATE IEMs to be much more comfortable that I had expected. If you check out my recent review of the Klipsch R6i In-Ear Headphones, you will see how I tear those apart for their lack of comfort. Well, I am pleased to say that the KZ-ATE is much more comfortable in my ears when compared to the R6i, and those are much more expensive headphones, so price is not always an indication of how good or comfortable an IEM will be.

CONCLUSION
The KZ-ATE IEMs are now my go-to IEMs when I want a fun and punchy sound on the go, that is, until my new Sennheiser IE80 arrives in the mail. Of course, the Senn's are much more expensive, and so if you want a cheap alternative to hi-fidelity IEMs with Earth-Shattering Bass, don't give it a second thought: The KZ-ATE is for you!! However, if you aren't a "bass head" and don't want to lose out on a whole $12, stay away from these.

review_text:
You Have To Be An Objectively Bad Person To Have A Problem With The Way These Sound. I'm a snobby, elitist audiophile. I'm broke, but that doesn't change the fact that I try so hard to enjoy myself that I can't actually enjoy myself. I have to police my thoughts in order to focus on the music and not the equipment playing it. I have really high standards and to cope with this purchase I kept my expectations very low. And I have been humbled.

Sound:
These sound good. Very good. Frustratingly good. I bought these because I already have some other iems and headphones (Fiio F5, Tin T4, SHP 9500's recently) but I needed something with a mic for use on PS4. I never actually intended to use them for music listening, I just needed something with a decent mic that didn't sound horrible. And I knew the KZ earphones have been getting cheaper and better for years, so I figured "why not."

Now I won't kid you, there are flaws in these *cough* $13 earphones. They're pretty V-shaped, and I noticed that some vocals were recessed (though the mids are still good. Perhaps it's right at the crossover point and only noticible in some songs. Regardless, my wife Lana Del Rey sounds good through them). Bass is excellent, punchy without being boomy, and I mean it! And the treble is bright but smooth. I'd say it's like a fine wine, but I don't drink, so I just have to assume it sounds like what wine tastes like.

Look, I know my review may not help you much, but that's the point. You don't NEED my help to know these sound good, you just NEED to buy them so you have an extra pair for quality earphones around the house. Granted, my Tin T4's are 10-20% better in key areas that make them worth spending $80 (honestly worth more imo), but the KZ ATE's are half way there! And they cost as much as two Starbucks orders!

So just do it. Pull the trigger. If it can make a no-fun snob like myself shut up, you're bound to like them too. 10/10, cannot believe they actually pulled off something this good for such an absurdly low price.

Oh, and the cable is alright too. Cheers.

review_text:
Why the hate for the ATE?. So if you look at the KZ earbuds generally they get great reviews with 4.5 ish stars. Yet the ATE gets 4 stars why? Some complain that it's tinny. Some complain that the fit is not good. Some complain that the build quality is not great. Let me address these one at a time.

The sound is Tinny: The pair I have sounded good to me. I believe most that get a tinny sound are having "fitment" issues. The foam is not the best quality and earbuds require a really good seal to get a "good" sound. For me the fitment is very good, but everyone has slightly different ears. Let me assure you if they can get a good seal the earbuds will produce a good sound.

The fit is not good: Once again this is the quality of the foam. if your canals can't get a good seal then yes the sound quality will suffer and the earbuds maybe loose. you can try the rubber pieces included, but really it is a matter of finding a manufacturer where you can get a "good" seal. The default foam tips fit me fine.

The build quality s not good: I do have to admit i have low hopes for this. The way the cables are hooked into the earbuds mean they go through some strain in normal operation. This is doubly so if you get a really good seal. The wires are NOT replaceable so after they break you will be replacing the whole set.

So why should you buy this? Well they sound great! If you do get a good seal (many many users do) then you will be rewarded. They are a great budget earbud, but keep in mind that they may not last as long as some others.

negative_points: low hopes for build quality due to cable strain

review_text:
You Get What You Pay For. If you want/need an inexpensive Bluetooth microphone headset this product fits the bill. I wouldn't recommend it for someone who spends the bulk of their time on the phone or on video conferences. The sound quality (both transmitting and receiving) is simply 'not there'. Sound coming into the headset is muffled and low, and never seems to be quite loud enough. In tests talking into the mic (both recording and speaking with a live person) the quality is (again) low and tinny. On the plus side, I love the ability to pair the headset to two devices (a phone and computer in my case). It means I can use one device for both phones and video conferences.

The build quality of the headset is quite nice. The plastic is nice and sturdy, and there's plenty of plush surfaces for a nice comfortable fit. I do wish the mic could be swiveled down farther, but the flexible arm allows me to position it where desired. Also, I'm not sure why the ear piece collapses/folds. It does nothing to make the headset more portable (i.e. save space), and is actually a little annoying.

Again, if you do a lot of phone/video conference work (more than once a day) then spring for a higher quality headset. However, if you just need something for the occasional call, either professionally or personally, then these should be fine.

Went through a dozen headphones before crowning the HD1/Momentum 2.0 king.. First, the HD1 headphones are simply the newer renamed version of the Momentum 2.0. Beginning in 2017, Sennheiser was forced to market the Momentum 2.0 under a new name, because it was found out that somebody else held the copyright to the name Momentum in the U.S. So, the Momentum 2.0 that is still for sale as "new" on Amazon is an older production run that ended in 2016, with some as old as 2014! If you're wondering what year your headphones were produced, look at the first four numbers of your serial number on the box. For example, 0445xxxxxx would indicate that your headphones were manufactured the 44th week of 2015.

I've tried or owned A LOT of other competitor headphones: Bang & Olufsen H6 (2nd gen), Bowers and Wilkins P7 and P9, Beyerdynamic DT-770 and Custom One Pro, V-Moda Crossfade M100, ATH-MSR7, Sony MDR-1A, etc.. With the HD1 you finally have a pair of headphones that has clear, prominent and detailed MIDRANGE, while also having a fantastic bass response, crisp treble presence, clarity, and imaging. With the midrange response on the HD1, vocals and other instruments sound more immediate and clear. Literally all other headphones I tried annoyingly scoop out the midrange response (usually around 1k) a few dB, with V-shaped EQs endeavoring to make the bass and treble response SEEM more impressive than it is. As a result vocals and instruments in that frequency range (like guitars) sound more distant and undefined on other headphones.

Lastly, you absolutely don't need an EQ or preamp with these headphones. Some audiophile types use pre-amps, DACs, and EQ to get the most out of high-end headphones, but I don't like to involve that kind of complexity. I want to just plug a great-sounding pair of headphones into ANY device (like my phone) and get an outstanding frequency response, fullness, and resolution. The HD1 does this all brilliantly. All while being very comfortable, providing outstanding passive sound-isolation, using genuine leather and looking very cool.

review_text:
Excellent and Super Comfortable Premium Headphones!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!. After reading various pro and customer reviews about how great these sound, I went ahead and bought myself the Sennheiser HD1 Over-Ear headphones (HPs) in the ivory color. The HD1 is the upgraded version of the Momentum 2.0 headphones by Sennheiser. They feature the exact same award-winning (2017) sound signature of the Momentum 2.0 headphones, but with added comfort. Sennheiser found out a year or so ago that the name "Momentum" was already trademarked, so they decided to rename this line to "HD1" in order to avoid a lawsuit.

Price: I paid $250 for these on Amazon + $25 tax, so a total of $275.

Looks/Design/Features: These are some really nice premium-looking HPs. Though the ear cups are plastic, the rest of the phone is all metal & genuine leather all the way! In between ear cups & the ear pads are gold metallic accents, which give the phone a more luxurious look. They are quite light, not bulky by any means, and so they are also quite portable. A big part of their portability also comes in the form of the "fold-in" feature (see pic below) which the original Momentum 1.0 did not have (though the 2.0 did).

The cable for the phone is a regular (non-braided) cable which features an in-line remote and mic. Though the phone is "Made for iOS", the only thing lost on Android phones with this remote is the volume feature really. The pause/play button works just fine, and I believe the same button can let you take and/or disconnect phone calls as well. The length is 1.4 meters, which is about 4.5 feet. I am happy with anything around 4 feet, so this is just fine with me. The part that connects into the HD1 features a "twist & lock" option as well, and it goes into the right side of the HD1. It takes a BIT of effort to twist and pull it out, but not too much really. I will prob just leave it in most of the time unless traveling long distances.

The HD1 also comes with a suede-like super-soft carrying case AS WELL AS a black hard case! Sennheiser held back nothing here! You usually don't get both, so this was a welcome surprise. The hard case has enough room in it so that you can even leave the cable connected into the HD1 w/o worrying about it (this is how they come actually too).

Comfort: I found these to be one of the most comfortable HPs I've ever worn! They remind me a lot of my old Sony MDR-1A 'phones actually, which were the most comfortable ones I've ever worn, though these may be equal to those or an extremely close second? Due to the HD1 being so light, and because of their smaller size, you don't have much pressure on any part of your head at any given time either. The headband is genuine leather with some padding on it. Not a ton, but the truth is it really doesn't need it IMO. The ear pads feel like giant super soft marshmallows against your ears. They had been enlarged since the Momentum 1.0 due to customer complaints, and it good to see that Sennheiser listened! Even with glasses on, these still felt super comfy to me! I have average-sized ears, and so I never felt my ears touching the speaker driver covering at all either.

The oval shape of these ear pads also have other advantages. One of which has to do with volume and potential hearing loss. Rounded ear pads let more of the sound leak out, which in turn forces the listener to raise the volume up, which can put the listener at increased risk for (unnecessary) hearing damage. But oval-shaped ear pads isolate sound better, and therefore less sound is likely to leak out, and the urge to raise the volume up higher vanishes immediately!

Sound: Many have said the HD1s sound great out of the box and don't need EQ'ing. For the MOST part I agree with this statement. They did sound great out of the box, but I felt they could sound even better, so I tried to come up with a custom EQ for the HD1s. But oddly enough it was the custom EQ I used for my now former Meze 99 Classics that made them sound their best! It opened up the sound to give it more "air" and also less congested (with respect to instrument separation) & less overly bassy on some songs as well. So these comments are based on the use of my Meze 99 Classics WITHOUT the Brainwavz ear pads custom EQs (1st set, 3 total), which can be found here. They were made for use in the Poweramp music app, so make sure to get that for best results! (See HD1 review on Head-Fi by RockStar2005 for these EQs)

review_text:
Not impressed. After reading dozens of reviews for over two years, in May 2018, I bought the Sennheiser HD1 headphone. The price then was $224. I was seriously considering the Oppo PM-3, but just about the time I was ready to pull the trigger, Oppo stopped making them. So I've had the HD1 now for a few months, and here are my impressions. Pros: The build quality seems to be good, and it is attractive. It comes with a nice soft bag as well as a very nice semi-hard, zippered travel case. Cons: The ear cups are a bit small for my medium-size ears. The headband is covered in leather, but has almost no padding. It puts pressure on the top of your head and becomes uncomfortable in short order. The cable is removeable, but is very difficult to disconnect. If you're comfortable leaving it connected, that wouldn't be a problem. Oddly, the volume control on the iOS cable is located at the upper end of the cable, only a few inches from the phone. The problem is it is so high you can't see it! You have to operate it by feel only. Bizarre. Lastly, the sound is disappointing. I can't single out any particular flaws--it's just not as good as I hoped it would be. Part of the problem, I'm sure, is that I'm using my iPad to drive it. It would probably sound better with a dedicated digital audio player (DAP) and higher quality audio files.

I didn't have the chance to try the HD1 before I bought it. If I had, I would have discovered some of the cons mentioned above and probably would have kept looking. I would advise anyone considering this headphone to definitely listen to it before you buy.

review_text:
Relaxed sound, forward mids, but bass and comfort have issues. Sennheiser HD1 Over Ear Headphones

Sound Quality:
· Bass is slightly emphasized over neutral, but nothing like the portable headphones offered by V-Moda or Beats. It's somewhat punchy, but could use more character and presence.
· Midrange is noticeably forward compared to other closed backs at this price. The midrange is clear, authentic, and spacious.
· Treble is very recessed and makes these a very easy listen and relaxing headphone, albeit not the most detailed. This lets the midrange shine even more.
· Soundstage is better than most closed backs I've tried, but still not great.

Comfort:
· The earpads are quite comfortable at first, but over time they become much less comfortable due to the memory foam getting compressed and losing it's shape. My ears ended up touching the drivers and the pads never felt secure and stable over my ears over time.
· Headphone is very lightweight and headband isn't even noticeable once these are on your head.

Build:
· Build is adequate. Lots of leather and stainless steel. The sliding mechanism does seem like it could come loose over time and the lightweightedness of these could make them more susceptible to drops. The build isn't a deterrent or a negative, but not a highlight either.

Overall, these are pretty good and better than M50x which are similar price on Amazon. I personally prefer more bass punch and more lower treble energy for a fun and vshaped headphone, but these definitely have a very specific sound that some people will love.

PROS:

· Lightweight, solid build
· Authentic, forward midrange
· Relaxing treble

CONS

· Bass could use more character
· Comfort degrades over time

review_text: Decent budget-friendly option but difficult for running without some MacGyvering. I bought these for running because they were the least expensive "active" bluetooth headphones I could find at the big electronics store I was at. My review is mixed. I have relatively small ears and a small head and these fit me very well. The sound/volume is fine for me when running, but I'm not someone who cares about great sound and probably wouldn't notice if the sound wasn't great. They typically have a brief, nearly unnoticeable sound drop about once or twice in my hour long run. I have run in the rain with no problems, and they keep working. The challenge is that the volume control/power piece bounces all over the place when I run and pulls the normally well-fitting earpieces out of my ears. I tried clipping it to my shirt, but the cord to the right ear isn't quite long enough and it pulled when I turned my head. Instead, I now clip it (and the extra cord length) to my hat. I use two sewing clips (my mom is a quilter and gave me some), which work perfectly when I use one on each side of the bulky control piece. I just can't take my hat off without pulling out the headphones, but that's not a problem for me. I don't regret the purchase given the low price and the fact that I figured something out, but I'll probably pay more next time to get something without a control piece that bounces.

review_text:
Bye Bye Bluetooth - ISOtunes brings the fire. Wow .. where do I begin? Should I start with the beautiful packaging or just get straight down to the meat and potatoes of the BEST headphones that have ever graced my ears.

I'd heard about ISOtunes before on social media (specifically Instagram) when a friend recommended I'd follow them. As someone who loves headphones and traveling, I'm always looking for the best new way to drown out the sound of airplane engines so I can rock out to my favorite tunes or hear every word of my Netflix shows. One problem with the previous ISOtunes headphones, I'm not a fan of bluetooth!

As someone who is old school in ways, I prefer to have the wires dangling around. That way there's a better chance I don't lose them and I don't have to connect them to bluetooth and hurt my phone battery. Anyway, back to the headphones at hand. When I saw ISOtunes come out with Wired Earplugs (for under $40, might I add), I sprung at the opportunity to purchase a pair, and boy did I make the right decision.

Wrapped up nice and neat when I took them out of the packaging, I properly followed the instruction manual (for once) to make sure I put the foam tips on properly without any problems. I went for the medium size but ISOtunes offers a large and a small so that it fits all ear shapes and sizes. Foam tips: check. Plugged in: check - It's time to test these babies out!

These aren't headphones if you're trying to blow out your ear drum. OSHA certified (which I googled, meaning they are safe to use at the workplace) make sure that the volume never gets too loud and hurt your ear. The sound was crystal clear, and the noise isolation was everything I expected and more. I powered up the TV in the other room to full volume, put the ISOtunes wired earplugs in my ears and seriously couldn't hear a word the TV was saying.

If you've made it this far, you're interested, so I'll keep the rest short. If you travel, work in loud places or simply need a solid pair of headphones for the morning commute, but hate bluetooth headphones, then these are worth every penny.

review_text:
Good choice for noisy shop environments. I am pleased with these earplug headphones. They are comfortable to wear for extended periods and they are very good at reducing the noise from my woodworking tools.

The sound is quite good and the bass is better than I expected. The volume is limited for a reason; it's a safety feature to prevent you from damaging you hearing. If you want to have the volume really loud in your ear then you will not be happy with these. But they are so good at cancelling the noise that you just don't need the volume very high to hear your music, or whatever you listen to.

Once you find the tip that you like, it's just a matter of learning how to properly put them your ear. There is a right and wrong way. The directions that are included explain the correct way to insert them to get the best noise reduction benefit.

The noise cancelling mike does a good job of allowing a caller to hear you over the noise in your environment. But they will have some trouble hearing you if you are standing very close to a very loud machine. I would never take or make a call while I was operating one of my tools, but I wanted to see how much noise these could actually block. So I turned on my loudest tool and made a call. I stood at various distances from the tool to see how well I could be heard. I could not be heard while standing right next to the tool, but when I took a couple of steps back from the tool, I could be heard much better, and the tool could not be heard at all. So I believe you could carry on a normal conversation while mowing the grass.

One additional tip: when you remove them from your ear, grasp the bottom of the foam plug. Otherwise you may cause it to be left in you ear. The tips are threaded but the insert that screws onto the post is only plastic.

review_text: Damaged box/didn’t work. Product arrived and looked like it had been slid around the floor. It was scratched and damaged. That along with seeing another language on the price tag (maybe it was Egyptian?) had me worried how these headphones would work. I plugged them into the charger and it flashed red and white several times, then a constant red. Then when it was charged it was white. I took it off the charger and tried to turn it on. It wouldn’t turn on. I’ve had my old pair for a couple years so I’m very familiar with how these should work and how to troubleshoot. Anything I tried would not help it to ever turn on. I appreciated being able to return these and get a full refund. I ended up buying some for the same price at Costco.

review_text:
Like i'm not even wearing headphones!. Most of the headphones I have dealt with in the past always have had a huge annoyance lurking somewhere. These Anker Spirits seems to have finally solved that. I think the most common annoyance I have had is fit and this is where these shine. Usually with a connected pair(wire between the two buds), the wire works its way to the left or right on my neck and tugs because it is too long or sits in the wrong spot. One of the best things about these is the small rubber chunk in the middle of the wire that allows the user to shorten the wire to any length of their choosing.(See Picture) Other buds after an hour or so make my ears throb and ache due to them putting pressure on some wrong part of my ear. These allows for the perfect adjustment of the wire prevent pull or discomfort. With the huge selection of included buds, I think anyone can find a good fit with these. For me personally, the default included buds with the little wrap-around piece fit PERFECT. I mostly use these outside doing yard work and I am blown away every time I use them at just how comfortable they are. After being outside for 3 hours, it is almost like they don't exist! Now that the comfort has been addressed lets get to the rest.

Sound quality: No these are not Sh*re monitors ($300-$500) but man are they awesome for what they are. There isn't a hint of muddiness in the highs and the bass is perfectly adequate for some gentle yard work listening. I would say 9/10 on sound comparing them to other ear buds in the same price range.

Battery Life: Honestly I don't know because they seem to never go dead. I have worked three 2-3 hour days in the yard without a charge and they just keep going and going and going.. like this bunny I know.. They seem to fully charge in a few hours at a charge rate of .25 amps and any sort of 30 min top up will give you plenty of juice for the rest of the day.

Durability: These are advertised as Ipx7 and boy do they live up to the hype. Even if you are doing hot yoga or some sweet Kung Fu in India at the height of Summer, these will hold up perfectly fine. As my pictures show I have no fears of submerging the entire device in a cup of water. The oleophobic coating (guessing oleophobic) keeps the water off and makes these seemingly impervious to the elements. The flap over the micro USB slot fits snugly and FINALLY has a pull tab so I don't need to get a knife to pop it off.

Overall for the price you pay, these are some of the best headphones in this category as far as I am concerned. 7/5 with rice, would recommend again.

Cheers

review_text:
Anker Customer Service Is Outstanding & SoundCore Spirit Pro Earphones Are Fantastic!. UPDATE 07/18/18: After my last update review of the SoundCore Spirit earphones, where I reported a serious problem with random, extremely loud screeching noise occurring without warning, I was contacted by Anker to resolve the problem. After providing them the details, they opted to send me a replacement set of earphones – and they went above and beyond by upgrading the replacement to the SoundCore Spirit Pro. Within a few days I had the replacement earphones in hand and have been using them everyday. There are some differences between the Spirit and Spirit Pro models, some small and some large. The Pro’s controls are tactilely different, the battery takes longer to charge, and I’m not getting quite as good a “seal” as I did with the Spirit model (I’m still fiddling with this so I’m anticipating the fit will improve as I tinker with the silicone ear tips). As compared to the Spirit, the Spirit Pro has a longer battery life, a nice balanced audio quality that sits just where I like it between treble and bass, and the Bluetooth range is simply phenomenal. The SoundCore Spirit Pro is one of the best wireless Bluetooth earphones I’ve used, and although I received mine as a replacement, if I were buying again I get the Pro model. Let’s talk Anker customer service. In a word – outstanding. In every respect, initial contact, responsiveness, follow-through, follow-up … just outstanding. For them to upgrade a replacement to a more capable model was above and beyond anything I was expecting. So, Anker SoundCore Spirit Pro earphones – a well-designed, high quality, feature rich, acoustically pleasing product backed by outstanding customer service. Could you ask for anything more? (OK, they give ‘em away free =8^) I’m very happy with my Anker products and recommend them highly. 2 Thumbs Up and 5 Stars!!

UPDATE 07/08/18: I originally rated this as one of the best products I've ever bought on Amazon and gave it 5 stars. After using them for several weeks a major flaw has surfaced and I'm forced to change my rating to 2 stars. The flaw? After I've worn these earphones for a couple of hours listening to podcasts or an audiobook on my iPhone, out of the blue without warning I hear an extremely loud screeching sound in both ears - so loud I have to jerk the earphones off. When this happens, not only is the sound deafening, the earphones disconnect from my iPhone. If I turn the earphones off and then back on and re-pair them with my iPhone I can listen for about another two hours before the process repeats. I really want to love these earphones, but having the pleasure experience of a podcast or audiobook rudely disrupted by an extremely loud screeching sound without warning just won't cut the muster. Thus, I must change my rating from 5 to 2 stars as these are not longer one of the most outstanding products I've ever bought on Amazon.

Original Review: I've been using these Anker earphones for about two weeks and they are flat out excellent in every respect. For the price these are hard to beat. Why? 8-hour battery life, very economical price, outstanding build quality, very comfortable fit, a neutral audio quality that is not too bass-heavy with highs that aren't "tinny" - just right, they produce good volume, and the Bluetooth range is incredible!. I've got a set of Bluetooth earphones by another manufacturer that I bought on Amazon, and they lack the range, the fit, and the battery life of these Anker earphones. I've listened to music of all genres, podcasts, audiobooks, TV programs, and more, and they all sound great. When I say the range on these earphones are incredible, I mean incredible. Most earphones like these have an effective range of maybe 25-30 feet before the signal drops out. With these Anker earphones I can leave my phone at one end of the house and go to the far opposite end of the house (at least 50 feet and maybe more) and the signal never fades, breaks up or drops. Incredible! With an 8-hour battery life I can work in the yard, garage, etc. virtually all day before the earphones stop working. This is very handy. I'd buy these again in a heartbeat. I've you're looking for a wireless Bluetooth earphone look no further .. these are what you want. This is one of the most outstanding products I've ever bought on Amazon, and if I could rate 'em 10 stars I would. 5 STARS!!!

review_text:
Definitely a great purchase if you’re on a budget. Before I begin the review, I want to note that I was planning on returning these earbuds if they didn’t meet my expectations and instead buying a pair of Jaybird x3’s. But, these met my expectations and exceeded them in some aspects.

When I first tried the earbuds I did notice that it sounded very flat and the sound quality lacked vibrance. Thankfully, there are built in eq’s into most streaming apps such as Spotify and Apple Music so I was able to adjust the sound to my liking. After doing so, I was pleasantly surprised with the amount of deep, rich base that was produced. Seriously, I wasn’t expecting it at all. The mids sounded pretty good and the highs were crisp and clear. To compare these to a common pair of earbuds, I would say that these produce much better base and highs than Apple earbuds, but the mids are just about the same if not a tad bit better. I would even go so far as to say these are just as good as the powerbeats which are $160. On the contrary, one thing that I did notice is that with certain songs, the mids lost a bit of clarity and the bass became somewhat overpowering. The sound will not blow you away, but it will definitely pleasantly surprise you. I mean after all these are $40 earbuds. Also, I wouldn’t call myself an audiophile, but I do have a great appreciation for sound quality.

The build quality exceeded my expectations. They have a nice, rugged feel to them. The magnets at the ends of the buds also provide a sercure hold. Also these buds come with an excess of accessories, so finding the right fit for you will not be a problem and they’re surprisingly comfortable. After 3 hours of usage my ears felt a little fatigue, but it wasn’t anything too terrible. One thing to note is that if you do not have the correct sized ear tips, there will be a great deal of audio quality lost. So even if the tips which come preinstalled seem to fit I would suggest trying other sizes just in case.

These are definitely sweatproof as I have used them in the gym and I sweat a good amount. They continue to work just as well as they did when I first tried them.

The battery life lasts for around 7-8 hours when the volume is 2 bars away from max. I havnt put that to the test yet, but I used these buds for about 3 1/2 hours and afterward they were just above 50%.

Bluetooth connectivity is also seamless and I heard no distortion from up to about 100ft away. I did not test this any further than that.

Overall, I would definitely recommend these earbuds to people who do not mind using Apple earbuds or other earbuds around and slightly above that sound quility range.

If there are any other aspects of this product that anyone wants me to review, feel free to ask. I will update this review after a week of usage.

review_text:
Spirit > Spirit X. The Soundcore Spirit is more of a 4.5 stars, but the Anker customer service earned the 5 stars. When I received the Soundcore Spirit, I can’t help but to compare it to the Spirit X. The box was slim and rectangular, whereas, the Spirit X was a cube. When I unboxed the contents of thr Spirit, we have similar accessories inside. A charging cable, various sized eartips and earwings as well as a small pouch for the earphones. The pouch feels like a high quality felt material. Also, I thought the snap close is a genius idea for a pouch. I have had other earphones that came with pouches, but all of them were closed by drawstrings. The Soundcore Spirit pouch requires the pinching of both ends of the opening to open and then it snaps back into place to close. So how does the Soundcore Spirit breakdown? Let’s see.

Sound:
One issue I had with the Spirit X model was that there was a hiss when connected to a source and music was playing. This hissing is most noticeable when the music is soft, which offen happens in classical music. When the music is pumping like say a dance track, the hissing gets drowned out. I was prepared for the Spirit earphones to have the same exact hissing issue. I powered it on, put on some music and kept listening for that hiss. It never surfaced. That’s good news.

Now for the sound, these earphones sound amazing for the price. The sound is clear and the BassUp technology works. I test my earphones with no equalizers and on a track like The Weeknd’s Starboy, the bass thumps. Look, I’m not one of those bass heads that need my earphones to dish out jaw jarring, core vibrating bass. I just want my earbuds to sound alive and these earphones does just that. I also switched over to Labrinth’s Jealous to listen to whether these earphones push the clarity and emotion of Labrinth’s vocals; it certainly does. Every type of music I threw at the Spirit, it passed the tests.

Let’s move onto noise isolation. It is decent on the NYC subway. While listening to podcasts I can hear the dialogue clearly with minimal external noises seeping in. I attribute the great noise isolation to the nice silicone eartips and the way the earphones sit pretty deep in the ear canal. You can probably improve the noise isolation even more if you purchase some Comply noise isolation foam tips… but honestly, you really don’t need to spend that money.

Comfort:
The Soundcore Spirit is small and light. Unlike the larger counterpart, I had no trouble putting these on. The earwings does a great job at keeping the earphones in place, which is needed for people working out with these buds.

Design:
The small profile of the earbuds with 8 hours play time is impressive. I still don’t like the wiring that runs behind the neck though, it still rubs on the collar of my dress shirt. Of course it wouldn’t be an issue if I used the Spirit with a t-shirt. The earbuds itself look good. The color way and the materials used, they all give off a high quality feel. The controls are simple to figure out. With bluetooth 5.0 and what Anker calls “sweat guard,” you can be sure these earphones will be able to handle the abuse you throw at it during your workouts.

Price:
The Anker Soundcore Spirit is priced the same MSRP as the Spirit X at $39.99. At MSRP, I will pick the Spirit over the Spirit X. Why? Because it is smaller, sounds the same and without the hiss, looks nicer and easy to put on.

review_text: Improved sound, battery life, and other features make this a great successor to the Soundbuds Slim+. Having owned the Soundbuds Slim+, this product comes as a marked improvement over the old model. The higher water resistance rating makes it more durable and now fully waterproof, and the new buttons are larger and easier to feel/press than the Slim+’s. An improved cable adjuster clip allows the extra wire to be shortened considerably in the shape of an 8 loop. The new battery cover is also easier to remove and turn around than before, as the cover now pulls out further and is free to move. After comparing the sound quality side by side across numerous genres of music, I noticed that the Slim+ is much more sibilant in the high-mids and treble and its bass is not as deep and tonal. I instantly noticed how much clearer and less painful the Spirit's treble upon listening to Vivaldi's Four Seasons back and forth on both pairs of headphones. Overall, I am satisfied with the improved sound quality and battery life over the Slim+, and the general design changes are a plus as well.

They are definitely more comfortable and there's less impact noise. Anker's customer service remains outstanding, though I've now had three pairs of their headphones in a month. Their "free" replacement policy is great, as long as you don't place any value on your time..***

These were suggested to me by Anker as a replacement for my previous pair of their headphone, the Soundcore Curve (which died after a month). They upsold me on the idea these the Spirits are better for running.

They're not.

I just took these on an initial outing, a five mile run. First, there's substantial wind noise even in a light breeze. Second, even the smallest tips seal too tightly in my ears. This causes two problems: (a) impact noise from your feet on pavement is omnipresent and (b) even at low volumes it's hard to hear, say, a cyclist letting you know they're coming up behind you. (c) there's weird suction noises as the phones move in and out of your increasingly sweaty ears. Third, the buttons are too close together to distinguish by feel while you're in motion. IMO, hooks over your ears is the way to go -- which is what my first Anker headphones had.

As far as sound goes, I listen to podcasts and books when I run, and they seem fine for that. I think the bass line of EDM along with the thump and whistle combo of my feet and the wind would drive me nuts.

On the upside -- and this is not nothing, and the basis for a 2nd star -- Anker's customer support was helpful and responsive. So, when these die in 30 days I'm sure I'll continue checking out their product line.

review_text:
Small flaws in design and overall experience mar an otherwise fantastic product. I love Anker products and they have a reputation for solid construction and quality, hence I bought these and honestly these live up to that standard. So why the negative review? Well, there's a few things.

First off, and maybe my main gripe is the fit. These simply aren't comfortable to me and may be one of the less comfortable headphones I've used, bluetooth or otherwise. Every possible combination of the provided tips and ear hooks just didnt feel like a tight or sealed fit, and as a result the headphones always felt kind of loose. i took these to the gym once and I can assure you that these stayed on and weren't loose in the slightest, so I was wrong on it being ACTUALLY loose, but that uncomfortableness was always there. After 5 days with these I gotta say I'm 50-50 on these and the fit hasn't gotten any better. Of course, that is 100% subjective and people's ears will vary greatly so make of that what you will.

Soundwise, these are decent. Bass, while not overbearing is tight and punchy and I noticed how clean drums sounded in most songs. Of course, much of the sound depends on a song's production but the sound was good or exceeding what was expected of the price point. That being said, I was getting a tunnel effect, especially on video content that made things sound "echo-y". Not a deal-breaker in of itself, but definitely a contributing factor to what soured me on these headphones. For reference, I'm using these with a Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge.

Moving on, Battery. The description says 8 hours of battery and having looked at laptops and all sorts of tech for years on end, I know that battery life always depends on how you use it and even what volume you listen at. So, I deducted an hour from the description and expected about 7 hours of battery life, which is about what I got. I got exactly what I expected walking in and came to the realization that it was a bit short for my preferences.

Finally, let's talk about the actual user experience. Pairing is nice and fast on this device and the little control dock or whatever you would call it on the headset is easy to use. 3 buttons, long press + for skip, tap for volume up. Long press - for replaying/ going back a song, and tap for volume down. Long press middle button for power, tap for pause. Oh, by the way, with the design of these, expect the headset to lean heavily to the right instead of the wire being evenly distributed towards both sides. All of these buttons worked great and it was such a relief to use a bluetooth headset with buttons that actually did what they were supposed to most of the time (looking at you JBL Everest). Range is fine but when I was out of range or at the very limit, the headset had an annoying tendency to fade in and out. Which brings us to the fading. The engineers or designers on this headset were apparently a little too fond of the fade in/out sound effect and used it for almost everything possible. Press volume up when the headset volume is maxed? Your music will now fade out, play a soft beep, and fade back in. It's kind of annoying. When the device's battery is low, it will fade out and beep every so often, enough to kind of get on my nerves.

And that's ultimately how I would describe these headphones, aggravating. They're a great pair for the price if you can get over these little grievances, and I have to admit that some of my problems listed above might seem petty or inconsequential. However, the poor fit is what did me in. You can have the most expensive headphones with 300000000000000000mm drivers or whatever but at the end of the day if they're not pleasant to wear then it's a bad experience. All of the other issues I possibly could have lived with but when added to the fit issue, I had to give these ones a pass.

EDIT/REVISIT- While the fit was initially terrible, it has grown on me and I would say that after forcing yourself to use these for a period, these may prove to be a decently comfortable set.

I also forgot to mention another thing and that is how heavily the set leans to the right. This is not noticeable at all if you use both ears but if you want to keep one ear in and the other out, you'll want to keep the right ear in since that's the side with the button panel. Not a big issue, but something that might be worth noting.

One HUGE thing worth bringing up is Anker's customer support. Those folks are beyond fantastic and would often reply to emails within an hour of me sending them. They were more than willing to work with me in any way possible and make my experience as pleasant as possible. One thing I can say is that if you;re unsure of a product but leaning towards trying it out, I'd say go for it. Their customer service is completely hassle-free and if you don't like it they'll be more than happy to help. Kudos to the folks over at Anker for the help.

review_text:
Bang for buck = excellent. I just received the Anker Soundcore Spirit Sports and wanted to share my initial impressions.
The packaging is a low budget attempt to be high end, which is fine. There are two boxes inside the package one contains the blue tooth headset and the other all the ancillary stuff (charging cable, books, ear tips of three sizes and 'ear wings' of two sizes.
I used the included Micro USB to charge them until the LED indicator went from red to blue, about :45 mins of me being anxious to get to try them out. While they charged I examined them carefully. They feel kinda cheap, if I'm being honest in comparison to my BeatsX that these replace. The wire containing the controls that connects the ear buds is surprisingly thin, which I think, in combination with the cheap plastic control box (again, coming from the machined aluminum of my BeatsX) is what makes up my impression of chintz.
Pairing was simple with my iPhone 7, power button for 3 seconds and bingo, there they are. They also show up in Control Center's battery section, which is nice.
Fit is very comfortable in my ears with the medium sized tips & small wings. I haven't used them other than sitting at my desk thus far so how they stay put while I'm moving around / running / etc remains to be seen. The body of these ear buds is more significant than my BeatsX and therefore they stick out of my ears about twice as far as the BeatsX, which I was able to wear under my full face motorcycle helmet comfortably (and get the helmet on without displacing the headphones), I seriously doubt that will be the case with these. No big deal as I really should be using my wired sound attenuating ear buds that are attached to my SENA blue tooth headset.
Sound Attenuation. This is important to me as I travel a lot and easily get annoyed by the inane conversations that I over hear while moving through the world. These seal into your ears nicely to produce a natural attenuation that feels similar to hearing protection I've used rated at -20db. Your mileage may vary as attenuation levels come down to how they fit in your ear a lot of the time.
Microphonics (the sound a cord transmits when bouncing around or rubbing against things) are very minimal, I put this down to the very slim cord.
Sound quality is pretty bass heavy. Even coming from BeatsX which are well understood to be bass-heavy. I used the "flat" eq setting on my iPhone with my BeatsX and enjoyed the slightly bass heavy sound. With the Anker / Soundcore Spirit Sports, I listened to Run The Jewels & Radiohead songs while messing with EQ settings to see where the sweet spot is for these. Many of the settings like R&B or Lounge are unpleasantly muffled and / or bass heavy. Flat EQ for music is slightly more bass heavy than I'd like - so I'll continue to play around here no doubt. I also tested the sound with one of my favorite podcasts, Do By Friday. Merlin's voice sounds great and overall, voices are clear and sound profile is good..Alex Cox's laugh is slightly less annoying through these headphones, somehow. Shrug.
Phone calls. Call quality overall is good. There is a more pronounced lag between invoking Siri or voice dictation for text messages than my BeatsX had - I'm assuming this is down to the W1 chip's magic.
Overall, like many Anker products, these headphones are excellent value for money.

review_text:
Comfortable, long lasting battery with full range of sound. Like many similarly styled earbuds from Anker before, the new SoundCore series offers more of the same..which is to say a great performing set of earbuds at a fair value over.

The fit is easily customized to fit different shape and size ears. There are separate pieces for your inner ear and ear loops to help get a fit that will stay in place no matter your activity. I found a fit for me that is comfortable over long periods of time. I have used them for everything from a short bike ride to a long car ride (using only one ear while driving of course - I use the included clip to attach the loose earbud to my shirt collar).

The most important feature of any earbud is the sound quality. I found the sound to be very clear and full - almost a little heavy on the bass for my tastes. I changed the EQ on my iPhone to reflect my audio preference and its been great for me. Audiobooks/podcasts can still be a little heavy on the low end but overall its a great sound. For music, I found the default EQ to be fine for me.

Bluetooth range is excellent. I can leave the phone on my desk and make it about 50 ft to the printer in my office without any issues. The included cable clips are an improvement over previous designs with the ability to reduce the slack on the cord between earbuds without having a hanging loop hit my neck. I haven't yet been able to find how long the battery lasts and that's because the battery life lasts so long. I use them almost every day and haven't had any problems with low battery warnings so that should be more than enough for most. I also tried to test out the water resistance of the earbuds and have been out in the rain wearing them and also put them in a cup of water to see if that would have any effect. Everything sounds and works as they day I first got them.

The remote/mic on the right ear is able to pick up my voice clearly. The button arrangement is pretty standard and very responsive to key press. I do have a preference for remotes that have a little more separation between them or perhaps a more definitive bump on the middle key to make choosing the middle button a little easier on first grab. That may be me just being nit-picky.

I don't think you can go wrong with the SoundCore Spirit. Anker has made it easy to get the right fit, great sound, and long lasting battery from a lightweight design and keeping the price affordable compared to other retail premium brands.

review_text:
A couple issues but overall a great option for casual/moderate users. I've had and been using these earphones for about 10 days now. I bought them at full price [$39.99] but I see now they have a $6 coupon :(. Ultimately, they are pretty good for the price.
Here's a breakdown of my thoughts on this product so far.

EarTips: These are very comfortable. I really love the shape of them, which makes them very secure but also, compared to the common hook shape of other sports earphones, makes it almost feel like you aren't wearing them.

Audio: The audio quality is decent; however, when it's connected to a device that isn't playing audio, the earphones often emit a sort of low droning static noise. I actually don't mind that part so much, because it can act as a minor active noise cancellation--in addition to the passive noise cancellation that is advertised and performs really well with snug (default for me) ear tips--which is helpful for when I'm in a focused studying mode.

Battery: I haven't actively timed how long these earphones last on a single charge continuously playing audio. However, I find myself having to charge these every night as, personally, I'm a heavy-user and use these (as my only pair of ear/headphones) constantly throughout the day. It'd be really nice if the earphones are useable while they are connected to the usb cable and charging, but they're not. [Please Anker R&D team make this happen for future versions!]

Bluetooth Connectivity: I do have an issue with its connectivity despite its Bluetooth 5.0. I haven't isolated any possible reason as of yet, but sometimes when I'm just outside the room of the connected device, 5-7+ feet away, the audio will sporadically fade-out for up to a few seconds before fading back in. It's a little frustrating.
** Edit: Customer support told me that "some Bluetooth signal obstacles will interfere the Bluetoooth range, such as walls, home appliances, wifi modem"; the fact that my connected device (Macbook Pro mid-2012) was a foot away from the wifi modem and I was testing the range from the laptop through a wall, lined with a fridge and oven, into the kitchen makes this issue understandable haha.

Also, sometimes the volume controls stop working both ways (on the earphones as well as if I try to control my volume from my connected computer/phone) so I have to turn off and reboot the earphones to fix that.

I really want to try out the Soundcore Spirit X and compare. Personally, I definitely would have benefited from the 4-hour extra battery life for the same price. I only hesitated and chose this Spirit Sports one because of the eartip shape since I wear glasses and thought it might feel weird having both hooks around the ear.

* Edit: Added a star because Anker has such fantastic customer support. Shout out to Emily who is simply amazing and very patient with me! They reached out to me really quickly and were willing to replace a possibly defective product, as well as answered any questions/issues I had. They take quality assurance very seriously, having me provide the serial/batch number printed on the cable of the earphones and a shipping label to return the defective ones after I got the replacements so that they can test issues further.

review_text:
Great value wireless earbuds. Today I am reviewing the Soundcore Spirit wireless bluetooth headphones by Anker. I have used a ton of budget bluetooth headphones over the years, and these earbuds include everything I'm looking for. They are basically my perfect pair of budget earbuds.

Design: They in ear portion is small with controls on a separate in line controller. I GREATLY prefer this to around the ear or around the neck earbuds with controls built into the ear portion or around the neck. So these are perfect for me in the design. Next up is build quality. Better than expected for the price. Not quite premium, but far better than "good enough". Also in regards to design is "fit". With 3 different sizes of tips and the rounded nub, these fit great and don't fall out.

Sound Quality and Mic: Listen, these aren't $500 Bose earbuds. That said for the current listed price of $40 on Amazon, these sound better than you would expect. They fall somewhere between "good enough" and "pretty good". Easily in the same quality range as name brand earbuds in the $70 to $100 range. Next and most important is mic quality. A lot of ear buds just use the worst mic they can find. This set however has an average mic and that's a big deal to me. No one complained about audio quality to me while on the phone.

SweatGuard: These earbuds include SweatGuard technology for sweat proofing. Now Anker reached out to me suggesting a salt water mixture to use to simulate sweat to test this. However, I personally don't care about test results and care WAY more about real world results. Thankfully for the purpose of this particular review, I sweat A LOT. So I had to do some yard work this past weekend and figured, this will be the perfect test. After a few hours of yard work with me absolutely drenched in sweat the headphones were still going strong. The sound was a little distorted until I wiped off the speaker part but then boom, back to normal. Couldn't be happier with how well they held up.

Other notes: Battery life is great so far. After a full charge I've probably used them for about 6 hours and they are still going. The box claims 8 hours, so at the very least that seems at least mostly accurate. The box doesn't claim any IPX raiting, yet on Amazon the listing title says IPX7, but the description then claims better than any IPX rating. If that's the case and it's better why not just get the rating and put it on the box? So something seems fishy there, but from a real world use I can tell you sweating profusely didn't damage them, and their simulated test method suggested I fully immerse them in the solution, so do seem to be actually waterproof despite no clear rating indicated.

Overall, at a current price of $40 these seem to hit the sweet spot. You can save a little but get a much worse product, or you can spend a little more and get a similar product just a different brand. You'd have to spend a good amount more to get an actually better product. I would definitely consider giving these a look if you are in the market.

review_text:
NOT worth $144 in any world. I'm not an snobby audiophile , but I can hear the difference between headphones. I'll go to stores and just listen to them to find the best bang for your buck.. I really LOVE music. I seen these headphones on Youtube various other articles and they were getting high praise, and even being compared to Beats by Dre headphone. I was in the market so I pulled the trigger and picked up a set!

When they arrived I was excited to try out this little know brand in hopes of finding a real deal in headphone.. I had them boxed up and ready to return about 2 hours later.

The noise cancellation HUMS and does not really cancel anything.. kind of dulls the highs in sounds. The hum is what was just the breaking point. You can hear it very well with no music playing and just a bit if you know its there.

Then there is the quality of sound. At low (with noise cancellation turned off!) and mid level volume the sound is pretty good. All ranges do fairly well overall. When you get to about 50% you start to get sound seepage to people close to you. This seepage, of course gets worse the louder you have your music. At full volume on an Iphone 7 plus, people across the room could sing along with you.. but then it goes into the next con to this headset. At max volume, the mids are distorted and the bass can't keep up with the volume and are lost in the overly loud mids.

As I said In the end I listened to these headphone for about two hours until I boxed them packed up and ready to return. Here is a snap shot of why.

Pros:
1. Low to mid volume sounds good
2. Build quality is nice and the headphone are fairly comfortable on the head.

Cons:
1. ANC (active noise cancellation) simply is garbage, it slightly muffles highs in the surrounding area. I was tapping a knife on the counter and when turned on the ting went away, but I could clearly hear every tap.. and ALL conversations are very audible.
2. The ANC has a hum when it is on. You can hear this in music, or just having them on your head.. very annoying.
3. At high volume mid range music and speech is distorted
4. At High volume music or speech, anyone withing 20 ft. can hear exactly what you are listening to.

The most I would pay for these headphone and not feel like I was ripped off was $60.. Perhaps the Ghost tek SoDrop (non noise cancellation) model would do better for the cost vs. quality.

I am not impressed with Ghost Tek at all.
